steps.title: Turn and Shape the Tail Feathers
steps.content: Turn the feather pieces right side out and press them flat. Lightly stuff if desired for extra dimension.

tip.text: Press carefully around narrow feather tips to maintain their shape.

steps.title: Assemble the Tail
steps.content: Gather the finished feathers into a fan arrangement and stitch them together at the base.

tip.text: Secure the feather bundle firmly because it receives frequent handling.

steps.title: Create the Wings
steps.content: Cut wing pieces from contrast fabrics, stitch right sides together and turn right side out.

tip.text: Topstitch around the wing edges for extra definition.

steps.title: Add Decorative Stitching
steps.content: Use embroidery thread to add decorative running stitches around the wings and body details.

tip.text: Contrasting thread colours help highlight decorative features.

steps.title: Attach the Wings
steps.content: Position the wings on both sides of the body and stitch them securely in place.

tip.text: Measure both sides to ensure the wings are attached evenly.

steps.title: Make the Beak and Wattle
steps.content: Cut and stitch the beak and decorative wattle pieces, then attach them to the head according to the template markings.

tip.text: Small hand stitches provide the neatest finish around facial features.

steps.title: Stuff the Hen
steps.content: Turn the body right side out and fill evenly with toy stuffing until the hen is plump and stable.

tip.text: Add stuffing gradually to avoid lumps and uneven shaping.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Fold the raw edges inward and close the turning gap with ladder stitch or small oversew stitches.

tip.text: A ladder stitch creates a nearly invisible seam.

steps.title: Add Button Eyes
steps.content: Sew two 10mm buttons onto the face to create the hen's eyes.

tip.text: For toys intended for very young children, replace buttons with embroidered eyes.

steps.title: Attach Ribbon Decoration
steps.content: Tie or stitch a light blue ribbon around the neck area as a decorative finishing touch.

tip.text: A small bow adds extra charm and complements floral fabrics.

steps.title: Final Finishing
steps.content: Check all seams, adjust the stuffing, straighten the tail feathers and wings, and remove any visible thread ends.

tip.text: Give the hen a final press around the fabric details for a polished appearance.

steps.title: Trim and Position Lace
steps.content: Cut lace trim to fit the sleeve openings and neckline. Position the lace between the fabric layers where indicated on the template.

tip.text: Baste the lace in place before sewing to prevent shifting.

steps.title: Construct the Arms
steps.content: Place the arm pieces right sides together with the lace sandwiched between layers. Sew around the shape, leaving the upper edge open for turning.

tip.text: Do not catch excess lace in the seam allowance.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff the Arms
steps.content: Clip the curves, turn the arms right side out and fill lightly with toy stuffing.

tip.text: Use small amounts of stuffing to keep the arms soft and flexible.

steps.title: Prepare the Legs
steps.content: Sew the leg sections according to the template markings, leaving the turning gap open.

tip.text: Keep the striped pattern aligned for a professional finish.

steps.title: Attach Lace to the Neckline
steps.content: Position the neck lace between the body and head pieces, ensuring the decorative edge faces inward toward the finished opening.

tip.text: Check the lace orientation before stitching the seam.

steps.title: Assemble the Body
steps.content: Layer the body sections right sides together. Stitch around the body, leaving the openings marked on the pattern for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Stretch jersey fabric gently while sewing to avoid distorted seams.

steps.title: Insert Arms and Legs
steps.content: Position the prepared arms and legs between the body layers according to the template markings. Sew securely across the attachment points.

tip.text: Double-check limb placement before sewing the final seams.

steps.title: Turn the Doll Right Side Out
steps.content: Carefully turn the doll through the opening. Push out the curves and corners gently.

tip.text: A blunt turning tool helps shape narrow sections without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Stuff the Doll
steps.content: Fill the body, head, arms and legs evenly with toy stuffing until the doll feels soft but holds its shape.

tip.text: Uneven stuffing can cause the doll to lean or twist.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning gap closed using small ladder stitches for an invisible finish.

tip.text: Match the thread colour to the fabric for the neatest result.

steps.title: Create the Face Panel
steps.content: Cut the circular dummy face piece from blue felt and position it on the front of the head.

tip.text: Pin the felt in place first to check the positioning.

steps.title: Add the Dummy

tip.text: For toys intended for young children, replace buttons with embroidered details for safety.

steps.title: Embroider the Facial Features
steps.content: Use brown embroidery thread to stitch the closed eyes and any additional facial details shown on the template.

tip.text: Draw the eye placement lightly with a fabric marker before stitching.

steps.title: Make the Hat
steps.content: Fold the hat piece right sides together and sew along the long edge. Turn right side out and press.

tip.text: Pressing the seam helps the hat sit neatly on the doll's head.

steps.title: Attach the Hat Trim
steps.content: Fold and stitch the lower edge of the hat according to the template markings to create a neat brim.

tip.text: Keep the folded edge even all the way around.

steps.title: Tie the Hat Knot
steps.content: Gather the top of the hat and tie a knot to create the signature sleepy cap shape.

tip.text: Avoid pulling the knot too tightly or the fabric may distort.

steps.title: Secure the Hat
steps.content: Place the completed hat on the doll's head and secure it with a few discreet hand stitches.

tip.text: Tack the hat at the sides and back so it stays in position.

steps.title: Final Finishing
steps.content: Inspect all seams, adjust the stuffing, trim loose threads and ensure every feature is securely attached.

tip.text: Gently reshape the doll by hand before displaying or gifting.

steps.title: Sew the Arms

steps.title: Stuff and Close the Arms
steps.content: Turn the arms right side out, stuff firmly but evenly, then close the openings with hand stitching.

tip.text: Use small amounts of stuffing at a time for smoother results.

steps.title: Construct the Legs
steps.content: Sew each pair of leg pieces together, leaving the top edge open. Turn and stuff the legs.

tip.text: Keep stuffing slightly firmer at the feet to help the doll sit properly.

steps.title: Create the Body
steps.content: Join the body pieces together according to the pattern markings, leaving openings for inserting the limbs.

tip.text: Check limb placement marks before sewing to ensure symmetry.

steps.title: Attach the Legs
steps.content: Insert the stuffed legs into the lower body opening and secure them with strong stitching.

tip.text: Double-stitch stress points for added durability.

steps.title: Attach the Arms

tip.text: Make sure both arms are aligned at the same height.

steps.title: Sew the Head

tip.text: Use smaller stitch lengths around curved facial areas.

steps.title: Stuff the Head
steps.content: Turn the head right side out and fill firmly with toy stuffing until smooth and rounded.

tip.text: Uneven stuffing can create lumps that are difficult to remove later.

steps.title: Join Head and Body

steps.title: Add Facial Features

tip.text: Pin facial features in place first and view from different angles before stitching.

steps.title: Prepare the Hair Yarn
steps.content: Cut multiple equal lengths of wool yarn for the hairstyle.

tip.text: Wrap yarn around a book to create uniform strands quickly.

steps.title: Create the Centre Parting
steps.content: Arrange the yarn strands along the centre of the head and stitch them securely in place.

tip.text: Keep the yarn evenly distributed to avoid gaps in the hairstyle.

steps.title: Make the Hair Buns
steps.content: Divide the yarn into two sections and twist each side into a bun shape. Stitch securely.

tip.text: Wrap the yarn tightly before stitching to maintain the bun shape.

steps.title: Cut the Dress Pieces
steps.content: Cut the bodice, sleeves, collar and skirt pieces from printed cotton fabric.

tip.text: Lightweight cotton fabrics gather more neatly for doll clothing.

steps.title: Construct the Bodice
steps.content: Sew the shoulder seams, attach sleeves and join the side seams of the bodice.

tip.text: Press seams frequently to improve accuracy and fit.

steps.title: Attach the Collar
steps.content: Fold and stitch the collar, then sew it neatly around the neckline.

tip.text: Clip the neckline seam allowance for a smoother finish.

steps.title: Gather the Skirt
steps.content: Run gathering stitches along the top edge of the skirt and pull the threads evenly.

tip.text: Uneven gathers can cause the dress to sit crookedly.

steps.title: Join Skirt and Bodice
steps.content: Match the gathers to the bodice width and stitch the skirt in place.

tip.text: Distribute gathers evenly before sewing the final seam.

steps.title: Finish the Dress
steps.content: Hem the skirt and finish all remaining raw edges. Turn the dress right side out and press.

tip.text: A careful press helps the dress hang beautifully on the doll.

steps.title: Dress the Doll
steps.content: Place the finished dress onto Jasmine and adjust the collar, sleeves and skirt.

tip.text: Use a small hand stitch at the back if you want the dress permanently attached.

steps.title: Create the Bow
steps.content: Cut a small rectangle of matching fabric, fold and stitch to create a decorative bow.

tip.text: Leftover dress fabric creates a coordinated finished look.

steps.title: Attach the Bow
steps.content: Secure the bow to the centre front of the hairstyle using stitches or fabric glue.

tip.text: Ensure the bow is firmly attached if the doll will be handled by children.

steps.title: Final Inspection
steps.content: Check all seams, facial features, hair and clothing. Trim loose threads and make final adjustments.

steps.title: Cut the Fabric Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Cut one outer sling piece, one lining piece, and one outer strap piece. From the remaining fabric, cut four rectangles for the straps. Fold each strap piece in half lengthwise and cut to create narrow strap sections.

tip.text: Check the size of the intended doll before cutting and enlarge or reduce the pattern if necessary.

steps.title: Prepare the Strap Sections
steps.content: Fold the strap pieces lengthwise with right sides together and stitch along the long edges. Turn right side out, press flat, and topstitch close to both edges for a neat finish.

tip.text: Twisted straps are difficult to correct later, so check orientation before stitching.

steps.title: Mark the Outer Sling
steps.content: Lay the outer sling piece right side up. Using a ruler and chalk pencil, mark the placement lines for the straps and press studs according to the template markings.

tip.text: Use a removable fabric marker to avoid visible marks on the finished project.

steps.title: Layer the Sling Pieces
steps.content: Place the lining fabric right sides together with the outer fabric. Position the wadding behind the lining layer. Align all edges carefully and pin securely.

tip.text: Ensure the wadding remains flat without folds to prevent bulky areas.

steps.title: Stitch Around the Sling
steps.content: Sew around the sling shape, leaving an opening along one side for turning. Trim the seam allowances, clip curved edges, and reduce bulk at the corners before turning.

tip.text: Clipping curves helps the sling maintain a smooth rounded shape after turning.

steps.title: Turn and Press
steps.content: Turn the sling right side out through the opening. Carefully push out the corners with a blunt turning tool and press the entire piece flat with an iron.

tip.text: Sharp tools can pierce the fabric when pushing out corners.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Fold the raw edges of the turning opening inward and stitch close to the edge. Press again to create a crisp professional finish.

tip.text: An edge stitch around the entire sling adds durability and improves appearance.

steps.title: Attach the Shoulder Straps
steps.content: Position the prepared straps on the marked placement lines. Secure each end firmly with several rows of stitching, ensuring the straps are evenly aligned.

tip.text: Uneven strap placement may cause the sling to sit crookedly when worn.

steps.title: Install the Press Studs
steps.content: Mark the locations for the press studs. Attach the male and female components securely so the front flap can open and close easily while holding the doll safely in place.

tip.text: Double-check stud orientation before attaching to avoid mismatched closures.

steps.title: Form the Carrier Pocket
steps.content: Fold the sling into its carrier shape and secure the side edges according to the template markings. Stitch carefully to create a pocket that comfortably supports the doll.

tip.text: Test the pocket depth with the doll before making final stitches.

steps.title: Adjust the Strap Length
steps.content: Fit the sling around the child's shoulder and check the strap positioning. Adjust if necessary to ensure the doll sits comfortably and securely.

tip.text: For younger children, shorten the straps slightly to keep the doll closer to the body.

steps.title: Finish the Doll Sling
steps.content: Inspect all seams, reinforce any stress points, trim loose threads, and give the sling a final press. The doll carrier is now ready for imaginative play.

tip.text: Always check that all stitching is secure before allowing children to use the sling.

steps.title: Print and Prepare the Templates
steps.content: Download and print the owl templates at full size. Carefully cut out all pattern pieces, including the owl body, eyes, beak, wings and decorative elements.

tip.text: Print templates on cardstock for easier tracing and more accurate cutting.

steps.title: Cut the Patchwork Panels
steps.content: Cut five fabric strips measuring approximately 5cm x 21cm from assorted patterned cotton fabrics. Arrange the strips in a pleasing color order to form the owl front panel.

tip.text: Alternate large and small prints to create visual balance in the finished owl.

steps.title: Join the Fabric Strips
steps.content: Place adjacent strips right sides together and stitch using a consistent seam allowance. Continue until all strips are joined into a single patchwork panel. Press seams open or to one side.

tip.text: Skipping pressing between seams can cause the patchwork panel to become uneven.

steps.title: Cut the Owl Body Shape
steps.content: Position the owl body template over the completed patchwork panel and cut out the front body piece. Repeat with coordinating fabric for the owl back if required.

tip.text: Center the most attractive fabric motifs where the owl's face will appear.

steps.title: Create the Eyes
steps.content: Cut two large eye circles from royal blue felt and two smaller circles from navy felt. Layer the circles and secure them with embroidery stitches around the edges.

tip.text: Use contrasting embroidery thread to make the eye details stand out.

steps.title: Attach the Eyes
steps.content: Position the layered felt eyes on the owl body front according to the template markings. Stitch securely by hand or machine around the edges.

tip.text: Check eye placement carefully before sewing, as uneven positioning can affect the owl's expression.

steps.title: Make the Heart Appliqué
steps.content: Cut a heart shape from pink felt and position it in the center of the owl body beneath the eyes. Stitch around the edge using blanket stitch or small running stitches.

tip.text: A hand-stitched blanket stitch adds a charming decorative finish.

steps.title: Create the Beak
steps.content: Cut a small beak shape from coordinating felt and place it between the eyes, just above the heart appliqué. Secure with neat hand stitches.

tip.text: Avoid making the beak too large, as it can overpower the face design.

steps.title: Prepare the Wings
steps.content: Cut wing pieces from patterned cotton fabric and layer them with matching wadding if desired. Stitch around the edges and turn right side out.

tip.text: Lightly quilt the wings before attaching for added texture.

steps.title: Attach the Wings
steps.content: Position the wings on either side of the owl body and stitch securely in place. Ensure both wings are aligned evenly.

tip.text: Uneven wing placement can make the finished owl appear lopsided.

steps.title: Assemble the Owl Body
steps.content: Place the front and back owl body pieces right sides together. Stitch around the outer edge, leaving an opening for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Leave a sufficiently large turning gap to avoid stressing the seams.

steps.title: Clip Curves and Turn
steps.content: Trim seam allowances and clip curved sections around the owl shape. Turn the owl right side out and gently shape the corners and curves.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to shape the ears and side curves neatly.

steps.title: Stuff the Owl
steps.content: Fill the owl evenly with toy stuffing until it reaches a firm but soft shape. Pay particular attention to the corners and ear areas.

tip.text: Overstuffing may distort the patchwork design and strain the seams.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning opening closed using a ladder stitch for an invisible finish. Smooth the stuffing and shape the owl evenly.

tip.text: Take small stitches for a professional-looking seam closure.

steps.title: Add Final Details
steps.content: Embroider decorative accents if desired and check that all appliqué pieces are secure. Give the owl a final press and shape before displaying or gifting.

tip.text: The owl template can be resized to create larger cushions or smaller decorative versions.

steps.title: Prepare the Templates
steps.content: Download and print the mouse templates at full size. Carefully cut out all pattern pieces, including the body, head, ears, hands, feet and side panels.

tip.text: If the pieces feel too small to sew comfortably, enlarge the template slightly before printing.

steps.title: Cut the Fabric Pieces
steps.content: Cut the body and head pieces from gingham fabric according to the template markings. Cut two ears, two hands and two feet from coordinating felt.

tip.text: Be sure to transfer all template notches accurately to help align the pieces later.

steps.title: Attach the First Ear
steps.content: Position one felt ear onto the front body piece at the marked location. Stitch securely in place using a narrow seam allowance.

tip.text: Pin the ear securely before stitching to prevent shifting.

steps.title: Attach the Second Ear
steps.content: Repeat the process with the second ear on the opposite side of the head. Ensure both ears are positioned evenly for a balanced appearance.

tip.text: Uneven ear placement will noticeably affect the finished mouse.

steps.title: Insert the Feet
steps.content: Place the felt feet onto the lower edge of the body pieces according to the template markings. Stitch them in place with the raw edges aligned.

tip.text: Check that both feet point in the same direction before sewing.

steps.title: Attach the Hands
steps.content: Position the felt hands on the body sides and secure them with stitching. The hands should sit symmetrically on each side of the mouse.

tip.text: Avoid placing the hands too high, as this can distort the mouse's proportions.

steps.title: Join the Body Pieces
steps.content: Place the body and head pieces right sides together. Stitch around the outline, leaving the base open and keeping a small turning gap as indicated on the template.

tip.text: Do not sew across the turning opening or stuffing will be difficult later.

steps.title: Sew the Base Section
steps.content: Attach the base piece to the lower edge of the mouse body. Carefully ease the curved edges together and stitch slowly around the shape.

tip.text: Clip small notches into curved seam allowances to help the base sit smoothly.

steps.title: Turn the Mouse Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the mouse through the opening left in the seam. Gently push out the ears, nose and body curves using a blunt turning tool.

tip.text: Avoid sharp tools that may pierce the fabric.

steps.title: Stuff the Mouse
steps.content: Fill the body evenly with polyester stuffing. Begin with the nose and head before working down into the body to create a smooth shape.

tip.text: Overfilling can stretch the seams and distort the mouse's silhouette.

steps.title: Insert the Tail
steps.content: Cut a length of cord and insert it into the opening at the back of the mouse. Secure the cord firmly with several reinforcing stitches.

tip.text: Knot the end of the cord inside the body for extra durability.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the remaining opening closed using a ladder stitch. Smooth the stuffing and shape the mouse evenly before finishing.

tip.text: Small invisible stitches will give the toy a professional finish.

steps.title: Embroider the Face
steps.content: Use black embroidery thread to stitch the eyes and nose. Create each eye with several small stitches and embroider the nose neatly at the tip of the snout.

tip.text: Mark the facial features lightly before stitching to keep them symmetrical.

steps.title: Add Final Details
steps.content: Check all seams and attached pieces, trim any loose threads and gently shape the toy. The finished mouse is now ready for play or display.

tip.text: Create a matching mouse in a different colorway to make a charming pair.

steps.title: Prepare the Templates
steps.content: Download and print the dinosaur mask templates at full size. Carefully cut out all pattern pieces for the Triceratops, T-Rex and Stegosaurus masks.

tip.text: Print onto cardstock for more durable templates that can be reused.

steps.title: Cut the Main Mask Shape
steps.content: Trace the chosen mask template onto felt and cut out the main mask piece. Mark all eye openings and placement guides.

tip.text: Transfer the markings before removing the paper template to avoid missing important details.

steps.title: Prepare the Interfacing
steps.content: Cut a matching piece of heavy-weight interfacing slightly smaller than the felt mask. This helps the mask hold its shape during wear.

tip.text: Trimming the interfacing a few millimetres smaller reduces bulk around the edges.

steps.title: Attach the Interfacing
steps.content: Position the interfacing on the back of the felt mask and secure it with fabric glue or temporary adhesive.

tip.text: Allow the glue to dry fully before continuing to prevent shifting while sewing.

steps.title: Cut the Eye Openings
steps.content: Carefully cut out the eye holes using sharp embroidery scissors. Keep the edges smooth and even.

tip.text: Avoid cutting beyond the marked lines, as enlarged eye holes may affect the fit.

steps.title: Create the Appliqué Pieces
steps.content: Cut all decorative features from contrasting felt colours, including horns, spikes, teeth, nostrils, cheeks and decorative spots.

tip.text: Keep small pieces grouped together to avoid losing them during assembly.

steps.title: Position the Decorations
steps.content: Arrange all appliqué pieces on the mask according to the template. Check the layout before securing them permanently.

tip.text: Take a quick photo of the arrangement before sewing so you can easily recreate it.

steps.title: Secure the Appliqué
steps.content: Stitch around the appliqué pieces using coordinating or contrasting thread. Use small stitches for neat edges.

tip.text: Keep stitches close to the edge to prevent the felt shapes from lifting over time.

steps.title: Add Embroidered Details
steps.content: Embroider facial features such as nostrils, wrinkles, scales, eyebrows and decorative markings onto the mask.

tip.text: Embroidery details help add dimension and personality to the dinosaur design.

steps.title: Create the Triceratops Horns
steps.content: For the Triceratops mask, cut horn pieces from white felt and stitch them securely to the mask front.

tip.text: Make sure the centre horn is aligned straight for a balanced appearance.

steps.title: Add T-Rex Features
steps.content: For the T-Rex mask, attach felt teeth, nostrils and facial details. Use embroidery stitches to define the expression.

tip.text: Vary stitch lengths slightly to create a more textured reptile look.

steps.title: Decorate the Stegosaurus Mask
steps.content: Attach decorative spots, spikes and facial details to the Stegosaurus mask. Embroider around selected shapes for extra texture.

tip.text: Layering different felt colours creates a more playful prehistoric design.

steps.title: Finish the Outer Edge
steps.content: Topstitch around the entire mask approximately 4–5mm from the edge to secure all layers and create a professional finish.

tip.text: Sew slowly around curves to maintain an even distance from the edge.

steps.title: Attach the Elastic
steps.content: Cut a length of elastic cord to fit comfortably around a child's head. Secure each end to the back of the mask with strong stitching.

tip.text: Test the elastic length before stitching permanently to ensure a comfortable fit.

steps.title: Add Final Touches
steps.content: Trim loose threads, check all appliqué pieces are secure and gently press the mask flat if needed. The dinosaur mask is now ready for imaginative play.

tip.text: Make all three dinosaur styles to create a fun prehistoric dress-up set.

steps.title: Prepare the Templates
steps.content: Download and print the fruit templates. Choose whether to make an apple or a pear and cut out all pattern pieces.

tip.text: Mix several coordinating fabric scraps to create a vibrant patchwork effect.

steps.title: Cut the Fabric Segments
steps.content: Using the template, cut the required number of fruit segments from assorted cotton fabrics. Transfer any markings before removing the templates.

tip.text: Keep all seam allowances consistent so the fruit shape remains symmetrical.

steps.title: Join the First Segments
steps.content: Place two fabric segments right sides together and sew along one curved edge. Press the seam open.

tip.text: Pressing after every seam helps the finished fruit sit smoothly.

steps.title: Create the Fruit Body
steps.content: Continue joining the remaining segments until all sections form a complete fruit shape. Leave a small opening for turning.

tip.text: Match the top and bottom points carefully to avoid twisting the shape.

steps.title: Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the fruit through the opening and gently push out the curves and points.

tip.text: A knitting needle or turning tool can help shape the narrow areas.

steps.title: Stuff the Fruit
steps.content: Fill the fruit firmly with toy stuffing until it becomes rounded and evenly shaped.

tip.text: Avoid overstuffing, which can stretch the seams and distort the patchwork.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning gap closed using small ladder stitches.

tip.text: Use matching thread so the closing seam becomes almost invisible.

steps.title: Shape the Top and Bottom
steps.content: Thread a strong piece of embroidery thread through the centre of the fruit from top to bottom and pull gently to create natural indentations.

tip.text: Pull gradually to avoid puckering the fabric excessively.

steps.title: Create the Stalk
steps.content: Cut a strip of fabric or ribbon and roll it tightly to form a stalk. Secure with stitches.

tip.text: A narrow fabric tube gives a more realistic stem than ribbon.

steps.title: Attach the Stalk
steps.content: Insert and stitch the stalk securely into the top indentation of the fruit.

tip.text: Ensure the stalk is centred before sewing permanently.

steps.title: Add Leaves
steps.content: Cut simple leaf shapes from coordinating fabric scraps. Fold and stitch them near the stalk.

tip.text: Use contrasting prints to make the leaves stand out.

steps.title: Make the Apple Variation
steps.content: For apples, use shorter, wider segments and create a rounded shape when stuffing.

tip.text: Bright, playful fabrics work especially well for apples.

steps.title: Make the Pear Variation
steps.content: For pears, shape the upper section narrower and the base fuller while stuffing to create the classic pear silhouette.

tip.text: Distribute stuffing carefully so the neck of the pear remains defined.

steps.title: Add Decorative Stitching
steps.content: Enhance the patchwork sections with decorative embroidery or topstitching if desired.

tip.text: Simple running stitches can highlight the patchwork panels beautifully.

steps.title: Finish and Display
steps.content: Trim any loose threads and arrange the completed apples and pears in a bowl, basket or display tray.

tip.text: These patchwork fruits also make charming drawer fresheners when lightly scented with lavender.

steps.title: Print the Template
steps.content: Download and print the Mother Goose Comforter template at full size. Cut out all pattern pieces accurately.

tip.text: Check printer settings are set to 100% scale before printing.

steps.title: Cut the Comforter Body
steps.content: Cut two body pieces from soft fleece fabric using the comforter template. Transfer any markings before removing the pattern.

tip.text: Choose a very soft fleece suitable for babies and young children.

steps.title: Prepare the Goose Head
steps.content: Cut two head pieces from cream fleece and two beak pieces from yellow fleece.

tip.text: Make sure the beak pieces are mirrored so they align correctly.

steps.title: Sew the Beak
steps.content: Place the beak pieces right sides together and stitch around the curved edges. Turn right side out and press lightly.

tip.text: Trim seam allowances before turning for smoother curves.

steps.title: Attach the Beak to the Head
steps.content: Position the completed beak between the head pieces and sew securely into the front opening.

tip.text: Ensure the beak is centred before stitching the head closed.

steps.title: Sew the Head
steps.content: Place the head pieces right sides together and stitch around the edge, leaving an opening at the neck.

tip.text: Do not stitch across the neck opening as it will be used for turning and attaching.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff the Head
steps.content: Turn the head right side out and fill firmly with toy stuffing until smooth and rounded.

tip.text: Add stuffing gradually to avoid lumps.

steps.title: Embroider the Eyes
steps.content: Use black embroidery thread to stitch simple eyes onto the goose head.

tip.text: Embroidery is safer than using buttons on baby comforters.

steps.title: Join the Comforter Body
steps.content: Place the two body pieces right sides together and stitch around the outer edge, leaving an opening for turning.

tip.text: Use a 1cm seam allowance throughout the project.

steps.title: Turn the Body Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the comforter body through the opening and carefully shape all curves and corners.

tip.text: Avoid pulling too hard on the fleece while turning.

steps.title: Close the Turning Gap
steps.content: Fold the raw edges inward and close the opening using ladder stitch or neat topstitching.

tip.text: Invisible ladder stitches provide a professional finish.

steps.title: Create the Goose Feet
steps.content: Cut four foot pieces from yellow fleece. Sew pairs together, turn right side out and lightly stuff.

tip.text: Only use a small amount of stuffing so the feet remain soft.

steps.title: Attach the Feet
steps.content: Position the feet evenly along the lower edge of the comforter and stitch securely in place.

tip.text: Reinforce the stitching because the feet may be frequently handled.

steps.title: Attach the Head
steps.content: Gather the neck opening of the comforter body and sew the stuffed goose head securely into position.

tip.text: Use several rows of stitching to ensure the head is firmly attached.

steps.title: Shape the Comforter
steps.content: Smooth the body fabric and gently arrange the gathers around the neck so the comforter drapes naturally.

tip.text: Even gathers create a more balanced and attractive finish.

steps.title: Check All Seams
steps.content: Inspect every seam and attachment point, especially around the head and feet.

tip.text: Baby comforters should have no loose threads or weak stitching.

steps.title: Finish the Comforter
steps.content: Trim loose threads and give the comforter a final inspection. The Mother Goose Comforter is now ready for cuddles and nap time.

tip.text: Prewash the finished comforter using a gentle detergent before gifting.

steps.title: Print and Prepare Templates
steps.content: Download and print the Hair Clip Dolly templates at full size. Cut out all template pieces accurately.

tip.text: Print at 100% scale to ensure the doll reaches the correct finished size.

steps.title: Trace the Face Design
steps.content: Use tracing paper and an embroidery transfer pencil to transfer the facial features onto the front head piece.

tip.text: Keep facial markings light so any remaining lines are easy to remove later.

steps.title: Embroider the Face
steps.content: Stitch the eyes, smile and cheeks using embroidery thread according to the transferred markings.

tip.text: Check both sides of the face before stitching to ensure the features are centred.

steps.title: Prepare the Head Pieces
steps.content: Cut the front and back head pieces from fabric and any required interfacing pieces for additional stability.

tip.text: Interfacing helps the head maintain a smooth shape when stuffed.

steps.title: Create the Hanging Loop
steps.content: Fold a length of ribbon into a loop and position it at the top of the back head piece.

tip.text: Ensure the loop is securely anchored because it will support the finished organizer.

steps.title: Sew the Head
steps.content: Place the head pieces right sides together and stitch around the outer edge, leaving an opening for turning.

tip.text: Do not stitch across the turning gap.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff the Head
steps.content: Turn the head right side out, shape the curves carefully and add stuffing until firm and smooth.

tip.text: Add stuffing gradually to avoid lumps around the cheeks.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning gap closed using neat ladder stitches.

tip.text: Ladder stitch creates an almost invisible seam.

steps.title: Prepare the Body Pieces
steps.content: Cut the front and back body sections from printed cotton fabric.

tip.text: Choose a cheerful print to make the organizer attractive in a child's room.

steps.title: Attach Decorative Trim
steps.content: Sew pom pom trim or decorative edging onto the front body piece before assembly.

tip.text: Keep trim aligned evenly to prevent twisting during construction.

steps.title: Add Storage Pockets
steps.content: Create and attach small fabric pockets to the front of the body for storing clips and accessories.

tip.text: Extra pockets provide useful storage for small hair bands and barrettes.

steps.title: Construct the Body
steps.content: Place the body pieces right sides together and sew around the edges, leaving an opening if stuffing is required.

tip.text: Match all seams carefully, especially around curved areas.

steps.title: Attach Head and Body
steps.content: Position the completed head above the body and stitch securely into place.

tip.text: Reinforce the neck seam with additional stitching for durability.

steps.title: Create the Hair
steps.content: Cut multiple lengths of wool yarn and attach them to the head, working from the centre parting outward.

tip.text: Use consistent yarn lengths for a neat and balanced hairstyle.

steps.title: Build Hair Volume
steps.content: Continue adding yarn rows until the head is fully covered and the desired thickness is achieved.

tip.text: Avoid leaving visible gaps between rows of yarn.

steps.title: Style the Hair
steps.content: Gather the yarn into pigtails, braids or another hairstyle and secure with ribbon bows.

tip.text: Bright ribbons help coordinate with the body fabric.

steps.title: Add Clip-Holding Ribbons
steps.content: Sew long ribbon lengths onto the hair to provide a place for storing hair clips and accessories.

tip.text: Attach ribbons securely because they will be used frequently.

steps.title: Final Assembly Check
steps.content: Inspect all seams, hair attachments, pockets and ribbons. Trim any loose threads.

tip.text: Test the hanging loop before use to ensure it supports the organizer safely.

steps.title: Print the Templates
steps.content: Download and print the Sprout Balls templates at full size. Carefully cut out all pattern pieces.

tip.text: Print at 100% scale to ensure all felt pieces fit together correctly.

steps.title: Cut the Felt Pieces
steps.content: Cut the ball sections from dark green felt and the leaf pieces from light green felt according to the templates.

tip.text: Cut smoothly around curved edges to make assembly easier.

steps.title: Transfer Facial Markings
steps.content: Mark the positions of eyes, smiles and decorative details onto the felt pieces.

tip.text: Use a disappearing fabric marker for accurate placement.

steps.title: Embroider the Faces
steps.content: Stitch smiling mouths, cheeks and any decorative facial details onto the front ball sections.

tip.text: Complete all embroidery before assembling the ball.

steps.title: Attach Safety Eyes
steps.content: Secure toy eyes to the embroidered face sections where indicated.

tip.text: Use embroidered eyes instead if the toy will be used by very young children.

steps.title: Join the First Ball Panels
steps.content: Place two ball sections right sides together and sew along one curved edge using a small seam allowance.

tip.text: Use small, even stitches for smooth curved seams.

steps.title: Continue Building the Ball
steps.content: Add additional body sections one at a time, sewing each curved edge to gradually form the spherical shape.

tip.text: Match the ends of each seam carefully to avoid puckering.

steps.title: Leave a Turning Gap
steps.content: When sewing the final sections together, leave a small opening for turning and filling.

tip.text: Do not make the opening too small or filling the ball will be difficult.

steps.title: Turn the Ball Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the felt ball through the opening and gently shape the seams with your fingers.

tip.text: A blunt turning tool can help push out curved sections neatly.

steps.title: Add Weight and Filling
steps.content: Fill the ball with dried pulses, rice or toy filling. Add enough material to create a pleasant juggling weight.

tip.text: A mixture of rice and toy filling creates a softer juggling ball.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the opening closed using small whip stitches or ladder stitch.

tip.text: Avoid overfilling, otherwise the opening may be difficult to close neatly.

steps.title: Prepare the Leaf Pieces
steps.content: Layer the light green felt leaves according to the template arrangement.

tip.text: Arrange the leaves before stitching to achieve a balanced look.

steps.title: Attach the Leaves
steps.content: Position the leaf sections around the top of the ball and stitch securely in place.

tip.text: Ensure stitches are secure because the leaves may be handled frequently.

steps.title: Add Decorative Stitching
steps.content: Use embroidery floss to add vein details and decorative accents to the leaves.

tip.text: Contrasting thread colours help the leaf details stand out.

steps.title: Shape the Sprout
steps.content: Gently fold and arrange the leaves around the ball so they resemble a Brussels sprout.

tip.text: Overlap leaf edges slightly for a more realistic appearance.

steps.title: Create Additional Sprouts
steps.content: Repeat the process to make a matching set of juggling sprout balls with different facial expressions.

tip.text: Vary the embroidered faces to give each sprout its own personality.

steps.title: Final Inspection
steps.content: Check all seams, facial features and leaf attachments. Trim any loose threads before use.

tip.text: Make sure all decorative elements are firmly attached before gifting or play.

steps.title: Prepare the Body
steps.content: Cut the body pieces from the fur fabric. Match the body sections right sides together and stitch around the edges, leaving the neck and back openings as indicated on the template. Turn right side out.

tip.text: Avoid sewing over turning gaps, otherwise stuffing and assembly will become difficult.

steps.title: Attach the Button Joints
steps.content: Position the button joints at the top of each leg. Stitch securely through the leg pieces and buttons, ensuring the joints are strong enough to allow movement.

tip.text: Pull the thread firmly but not excessively, as too much tension can distort the fabric.

steps.title: Join Legs to the Body
steps.content: Insert the completed legs into the lower body opening. Align the button joints with the marked positions and stitch securely so the legs can move while remaining firmly attached.

tip.text: Check that both legs are level before securing the final stitches.

steps.title: Make and Attach the Arms
steps.content: Cut arm pieces from fur fabric and sew each pair together, leaving an opening for turning. Turn right side out, lightly stuff and attach button joints. Secure the arms to the body at the marked positions.

tip.text: Use a chopstick or stuffing tool to shape the ends of the arms neatly.

steps.title: Construct the Head
steps.content: Sew the head pieces together following the template markings. Leave an opening for turning and stuffing. Turn right side out and begin filling the head firmly to create a rounded teddy bear shape.

tip.text: Uneven stuffing can cause lumps and make facial features appear crooked.

steps.title: Add Eyes and Nose
steps.content: Attach the toy eyes and nose in the marked positions. If making the bear for a young child, embroider the eyes instead. Check symmetry before securing permanently.

tip.text: Safety eyes are not recommended for very young children unless securely fitted according to manufacturer instructions.

steps.title: Attach the Head
steps.content: Position the stuffed head onto the neck opening of the body. Use small ladder stitches to sew the head securely in place, ensuring it faces forward.

tip.text: A loosely attached head may wobble, so reinforce the neck area with extra stitches.

steps.title: Stuff and Close the Body
steps.content: Fill the body with polyester toy stuffing until firm and evenly shaped. Close the remaining opening with invisible hand stitches.

tip.text: Add stuffing gradually and shape the body as you work for a more professional finish.

steps.title: Add Finishing Details
steps.content: Tie a ribbon around the teddy bear's neck and make any final adjustments to the fur, stuffing and facial features. Trim loose threads and groom the curly fur for a neat appearance.

tip.text: Use a soft brush to gently fluff the fur and bring out its curly texture.

steps.title: Prepare the Pattern Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the pattern templates. Cut all fabric, felt, wadding and interfacing pieces according to the pattern guide. Transfer any placement markings onto the fabric.

tip.text: Label each piece after cutting to keep track of the kit bag sections and medical accessories.

steps.title: Apply Interfacing and Wadding
steps.content: Attach interfacing to the main fabric pieces and layer wadding where indicated. Baste the layers together to prevent shifting during construction.

tip.text: Smooth out wrinkles before basting to achieve a professional finish.

steps.title: Create the Medical Symbols
steps.content: Cut red and white felt pieces for the first aid cross motifs. Position them on the bag and accessory pieces and secure with appliqué stitching or embroidery.

tip.text: Check alignment before stitching, as off-centre crosses are difficult to correct later.

steps.title: Construct the First Aid Bag Panels
steps.content: Sew the front, back and side panels together with right sides facing. Press seams open and reinforce stress points with additional stitching.

tip.text: Use clips instead of pins when sewing through multiple padded layers.

steps.title: Add the Bag Closure
steps.content: Create the opening flap or closure section following the pattern markings. Attach any fastening components before assembling the final bag.

tip.text: Ensure closures are securely attached, especially if the toy will be used frequently.

steps.title: Bind the Edges
steps.content: Apply red bias binding around the required edges to create a neat and durable finish. Stitch carefully around corners and curves.

tip.text: Use fabric clips to hold the binding in place while sewing.

steps.title: Make the Toy Bandage
steps.content: Cut the bandage fabric strip and sew the layers together. Turn right side out, press flat and add the felt medical cross detail to the centre.

tip.text: Topstitch around the bandage edge to help it keep its shape.

steps.title: Create the Toy Medical Accessories
steps.content: Sew the remaining first aid accessories included in the set, such as toy medicine bottles, instruments or treatment items. Lightly stuff pieces where required.

tip.text: Avoid overstuffing small accessories as they can become bulky and difficult to fit inside the bag.

steps.title: Assemble and Fill the Kit
steps.content: Place all completed medical accessories inside the first aid bag. Check that the bag opens and closes easily and that all items fit comfortably.

tip.text: Arrange larger items at the bottom to help the bag keep its shape.

steps.title: Finish and Inspect
steps.content: Trim loose threads, inspect all seams and reinforce any areas that receive frequent handling. Give the completed first aid kit a final press before use.

tip.text: This project may contain small parts and is not suitable for children under three years old.

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Head Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Add a 5mm seam allowance to all pieces. Cut two ear pieces from lightly patterned fabric and two more from another print. Pair the ear pieces with right sides together, sew around the curved edges, and leave an opening for turning. Turn right side out, press, insert wadding, and close the opening with neat hand stitches.

tip.text: Press the seams carefully before turning the ears to create crisp edges and a professional finish.

steps.title: Create the Head Shape
steps.content: Cut the head pieces from fabric and transfer all markings. Sew the darts and shape seams as indicated on the template. Stitch the head pieces together, leaving an opening for turning and stuffing. Turn right side out and fill firmly with toy stuffing.

tip.text: Understuffing the head can make the facial features appear uneven once embroidered.

steps.title: Make and Attach the Legs
steps.content: Cut four leg pieces from patterned fabric. Sew pairs together, leaving a gap at the top edge. Clip curved areas, turn right side out, and stuff firmly. Fold the leg openings inward and stitch closed. Position the legs at the base of the body and secure in place.

tip.text: Avoid overfilling the legs, as bulky seams can make assembly difficult.

steps.title: Construct the Arms
steps.content: Cut four arm pieces from coordinating fabric. Sew around the outer edges, leaving a small turning gap. Turn right side out, stuff lightly, and close the openings. Prepare the arms for button-jointed attachment later.

tip.text: Keep the upper arm area lightly stuffed so the joints can move more naturally.

steps.title: Assemble the Body
steps.content: Cut the body pieces and sew them together following the template markings. Insert the legs into position while sewing the lower seams. Turn the body right side out through the opening and stuff firmly before closing the gap.

tip.text: Check that both legs are aligned evenly before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Attach the Arms with Button Joints
steps.content: Using a long needle and embroidery thread, attach the arms through the body with button joints. Pass the needle through one arm, across the body, and through the second arm. Secure with buttons and tighten until the arms move freely.

tip.text: Test the arm movement before tying off the thread to ensure both sides rotate smoothly.

steps.title: Embroider the Face
steps.content: Embroider the nose using satin stitches and add a vertical stitch detail along the back. Position and sew the bead eyes securely. Shape the face gently by tightening stitches around the nose area and secure all thread ends neatly.

tip.text: Uneven eye placement can dramatically affect the hare’s expression, so mark positions carefully first.

steps.title: Create the Tail
steps.content: Make a small pom-pom using white yarn. Trim it into a neat round shape and stitch it securely to the back of the hare.

tip.text: Use extra stitching through the center of the pom-pom to prevent it loosening over time.

steps.title: Sew the Dress Bodice
steps.content: Cut bodice pieces from folded fabric and lining. Sew the shoulder seams, attach the lining, clip curves, and turn right side out. Press thoroughly and topstitch where required.

tip.text: Clip neckline curves before turning to avoid puckering around the bodice edge.

steps.title: Make the Skirt
steps.content: Cut contrasting fabric for the skirt panels. Sew the side seams, gather the top edge evenly, and attach the skirt to the bodice. Add lace trim and decorative details as desired.

tip.text: Distribute gathers evenly before stitching to create a balanced skirt shape.

steps.title: Finish the Dress
steps.content: Attach the lining, add snap fasteners to the back opening, and complete all hems. Press the finished dress and check that it fits comfortably over the hare.

tip.text: Installing snaps too close to the fabric edge can weaken the closure over time.

steps.title: Dress and Finish Harriet Hare
steps.content: Put the completed dress onto the hare, fasten the snaps, adjust the ears, and smooth the stuffing. Check all seams and embellishments before displaying or gifting the finished toy.

tip.text: Ensure all beads, buttons, and decorative elements are securely attached if the toy will be handled frequently.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Patterned fat quarters and plain cotton fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:

Plain cotton fabric.
Fibre filling.
Buttons for eyes.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Toy Making, Machine Sewing, Hand Sewing, Stuffing, Topstitching

steps.title: Prepare the Templates
steps.content: Download, print and cut out all template pieces. Trace the shapes onto thin card to create durable pattern templates for repeated use.

tip.text: Card templates make it easier to trace accurate shapes onto fabric.

steps.title: Transfer the Pattern
steps.content: Place the templates onto the reverse side of the chosen fabrics and trace around them carefully. Add a 5mm seam allowance around all pieces.

tip.text: Forgetting seam allowances can make the finished dolphin noticeably smaller.

steps.title: Cut the Fabric Pieces
steps.content: Cut one gusset, one tail and two fin pieces from the lighter fabric. Cut two body pieces and two tail-fin pieces from the darker patterned fabric.

tip.text: Use sharp fabric scissors to keep curved edges smooth and accurate.

steps.title: Layer the Tail and Fin Pieces
steps.content: Match the dark and light tail-fin pieces right sides together and place quilt wadding or stabilizing layer between them if desired.

tip.text: Pin curved sections generously to prevent shifting while sewing.

steps.title: Sew the Tail Fins
steps.content: Stitch around the tail-fin shapes, leaving the turning edge open. Trim excess fabric from the curves before turning.

tip.text: Not trimming curved seam allowances can create bulky, uneven edges.

steps.title: Turn and Topstitch the Tail
steps.content: Turn the tail-fin pieces right side out and press flat. Topstitch around the edges to create a neat finished appearance.

tip.text: A slightly longer stitch length gives decorative topstitching a cleaner look.

steps.title: Attach the Side Fins
steps.content: Position the side fins on the body pieces using the template markings. Secure them temporarily with tacking stitches.

tip.text: Check that both fins mirror each other before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Prepare the Body
steps.content: Place the two body pieces right sides together and align all markings carefully before sewing.

tip.text: Matching the nose and tail points accurately improves the final shape.

steps.title: Insert the Gusset
steps.content: Position the gusset between the body pieces and pin around the curved edges, easing the fabric gently where necessary.

tip.text: Pulling the fabric while easing curves may distort the dolphin's shape.

steps.title: Sew the Dolphin Body
steps.content: Stitch around the entire body, securing the fins and gusset in place. Leave a gap for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Do not sew the turning opening closed by mistake.

steps.title: Clip the Curves
steps.content: Clip seam allowances around the nose, tail and curved sections to reduce bulk and improve shaping.

tip.text: Take care not to cut through the stitching line.

steps.title: Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Carefully turn the dolphin through the opening and push out the nose and tail points using a blunt turning tool.

tip.text: A chopstick or point turner helps shape narrow areas without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Shape and Press
steps.content: Gently smooth all seams with your fingers and press lightly if the fabric allows.

tip.text: Finger-pressing curved seams before ironing often gives better results.

steps.title: Stuff the Dolphin
steps.content: Fill the body firmly with fibre filling, paying particular attention to the nose and tail areas to achieve a smooth shape.

tip.text: Large handfuls of stuffing can create lumps inside the toy.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Fold the seam allowance of the opening inward and close it neatly with small oversew or ladder stitches.

tip.text: Matching thread color helps make the closing stitches nearly invisible.

steps.title: Attach the Tail
steps.content: Position the completed tail section at the rear opening and secure it firmly with hand stitching.

tip.text: Reinforce the tail attachment because it is frequently handled.

steps.title: Add the Eyes
steps.content: Sew a small black button onto each side of the dolphin's head to create the eyes.

tip.text: Buttons may present a choking hazard for children under three years old.

steps.title: Final Inspection
steps.content: Check all seams, attachments and shaping. Add extra stuffing if needed and trim any loose threads before displaying or gifting the dolphin.

tip.text: Give the dolphin a final squeeze and reshape the stuffing for a polished finish.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Printed and plain cotton fat quarters

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Fabric, fat quarters, cotton: printed and plain.
Fibre filling.
Lightweight quilt wadding.
Pale pink pencil.
5mm seam allowance used throughout unless otherwise stated.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Stuffing, Sewing, Embroidery

steps.title: Create the Head and Body
steps.content: Print and cut the templates. Cut one full body shape and one lower body shape from printed fabric. Sew the lower body to the neck section to create a complete body piece. Place the body pieces right sides together and stitch around the outline, leaving a small opening at the side for turning. Clip curves, turn right side out, stuff firmly, then close the opening with slip stitches. Sketch facial features with a soft pencil and embroider the face using embroidery thread. Add pale pink cheeks with a pencil.

tip.text: Add stuffing gradually around the neck and head area to create a smooth shape without lumps.

steps.title: Make and Attach the Arms
steps.content: Cut two arm pieces from contrasting fabric and one matching piece from lightweight quilt wadding. Layer the fabrics and wadding together, stitch around the arm shape leaving a turning gap, then turn right side out and press. Fold the raw edges inside the gap and close neatly. Wrap the finished arms around the doll’s body so the hands overlap and secure in place. Oversew the arm wrap to the body, beginning and ending approximately 1cm from the side seams.

tip.text: Positioning the arms unevenly can make the doll appear unbalanced when displayed.

steps.title: Sew the Headscarf
steps.content: Cut headscarf pieces from two coordinating fabrics. Stitch right sides together, leaving a small opening at the bottom centre. Turn right side out, press flat and topstitch close to the edge. Position the scarf across the forehead and secure one edge to the back of the head. Fold the top edge toward the centre, pin the ties in place and stitch the lower edges to the sides of the face.

tip.text: Press the scarf thoroughly before attaching it to achieve crisp edges and a neat finish.

steps.title: Create the Bow
steps.content: Cut a strip of fabric measuring approximately 5cm square and fold it in half right sides together. Sew along the edge, turn right side out and move the seam to the centre. Open the tie ends from the middle of the head and thread them through the loops on either side. Slip-stitch the loop to the top centre of the forehead and tuck the ends back through the loop to form a decorative bow.

tip.text: Adjust the bow loops before securing the stitches to create a symmetrical finish.

steps.title: Prepare the Deer Mask Face
steps.content: Download and print the template. Use the photographs as a colour guide. Cut out the deer face template, trace onto felt and carefully cut out the main face shape.

tip.text: Use a water-erasable pen to transfer markings accurately without leaving permanent lines.

steps.title: Cut the Deer Features
steps.content: Cut the central V-shaped band, inner ears, nose, cheeks and eyelash pieces from contrasting felt colours according to the template markings.

tip.text: Keep small felt pieces grouped together to avoid mixing up mirrored parts.

steps.title: Assemble the Deer Face
steps.content: Position the decorative felt pieces onto the deer face. Glue the inner ears, nose and cheeks in place, leaving the eyelashes separate until later.

tip.text: Apply only a small amount of glue to prevent the felt from becoming stiff.

steps.title: Add Interfacing Support
steps.content: Cut a piece of pelmet interfacing slightly larger than the mask. Layer the felt face over the interfacing and secure with small dabs of glue.

tip.text: Interfacing gives the mask structure and helps it hold its shape during wear.

steps.title: Stitch and Finish the Deer Mask
steps.content: Machine stitch around all decorative pieces close to the edges. Cut out the eye openings through all layers, attach the eyelashes and stitch decorative details around the face.

tip.text: Cut eye openings gradually and test fit often to avoid making them too large.

steps.title: Attach the Elastic
steps.content: Insert the ends of the elastic into the marked positions at the sides of the mask. Stitch securely around the outer edge and topstitch decorative details.

tip.text: Backstitch over the elastic ends several times to ensure they can withstand play.

steps.title: Make the Fox Mask
steps.content: Cut the fox face, ears, cheeks, nose and side pieces from felt. Assemble the layers following the same method used for the deer mask and stitch all details in place.

tip.text: Arrange all pieces before stitching to confirm colour placement and symmetry.

steps.title: Prepare the Hedgehog Mask
steps.content: Cut the hedgehog face, head and ruff sections from coloured felt. Transfer eye markings and prepare the decorative elements.

tip.text: Ensure the ruff is centred evenly around the face before securing it.

steps.title: Assemble the Hedgehog Layers
steps.content: Layer the face, interfacing and ruff pieces. Secure with glue and stitch around the face opening and decorative details before cutting out the eye holes.

tip.text: Stitch slowly around curves for smoother, cleaner edges.

steps.title: Finish the Hedgehog Mask
steps.content: Attach the elastic ends, sew around the outer edge and add the nose and ear details. Secure all stitching and trim any loose threads.

tip.text: Check all embellishments are firmly attached before giving the mask to a child.

steps.title: Prepare the Pattern Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Transfer the forehead, front head, back head and body pieces onto your chosen fabrics. Cut out all pieces, adding a 5mm seam allowance where required.

tip.text: Label each fabric piece before cutting to make assembly easier later.

steps.title: Sew the Head Front
steps.content: Place the forehead and front head pieces right sides together. Stitch the forehead to the front head, matching all markings and notches carefully.

tip.text: Misaligned notches can distort the deer’s face shape, so match them carefully before sewing.

steps.title: Add Facial Features
steps.content: Insert the safety eyes or embroider the eyes using French knots. Embroider the eyelashes, nose and mouth with embroidery thread.

tip.text: If making the toy for a young child, embroidered eyes are safer than plastic safety eyes.

steps.title: Create the Hooves
steps.content: Join contrasting fabrics together and use the arm and leg templates to cut the hoof sections. Stitch the pieces together and prepare the limbs.

tip.text: Press seams open before cutting template pieces for cleaner, more accurate shapes.

steps.title: Sew and Stuff the Legs
steps.content: Sew around the leg markings, leaving the tops open. Trim the seams, turn right side out and add a small amount of stuffing to each leg.

tip.text: Overstuffing the legs can make attaching them to the body more difficult.

steps.title: Make the Ears
steps.content: Sew the ear pieces together, leaving the lower edge open. Trim, turn right side out and secure the shape with a few small stitches.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to shape the ear tips without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Assemble the Head
steps.content: Position the ears on the embroidered head piece. Place the back head section on top with right sides together and sew around the head, leaving the neck opening free.

tip.text: Check the ears are facing inward before stitching the head closed.

steps.title: Stuff and Close the Head
steps.content: Turn the head right side out and fill firmly with stuffing. Gather the neck opening and close securely with hand stitches.

tip.text: Secure the closing stitches firmly because the head will support handling and play.

steps.title: Attach the Legs
steps.content: Lay the body piece flat and position the legs according to the template markings. Tack them in place before sewing the body.

tip.text: Double-check leg placement so the finished deer sits evenly.

steps.title: Sew the Body
steps.content: Place the second body piece on top, right sides together. Stitch around the body, leaving the neck opening free.

tip.text: Avoid catching the legs in unwanted seams while sewing around the body.

steps.title: Finish the Deer
steps.content: Turn the body right side out, fill with stuffing and close the opening. Attach the head securely to the body using strong hand stitches.

tip.text: Reinforce the neck connection with extra stitches for durability.

steps.title: Make the Scarf
steps.content: Cut a rectangle measuring 5cm x 40cm. Fold lengthwise and sew along the long edge, leaving a small turning gap. Turn right side out, close the gap and press flat.

tip.text: A loop turner makes turning narrow scarf pieces much easier.

steps.title: Create the Shorts
steps.content: Fold fabric in half and cut two shorts pieces from the template. Sew the leg seams and join the sections according to the pattern markings.

tip.text: Keep track of right and left pieces to avoid twisting the shorts during assembly.

steps.title: Fit the Outfit
steps.content: Turn the shorts right side out and fit them onto the deer. Tie the scarf around the neck and adjust all clothing pieces for the finished look.

tip.text: Lightly press the outfit before dressing the deer for a professional finish.

steps.title: Prepare the Pattern Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the template. Cut two wings from patterned fabric and one wing layer from wadding. Cut four leg pieces from patterned fabric and two body pieces, four arm pieces and four leg pieces from plain cotton.

tip.text: Mark all pattern pieces before cutting to avoid confusion during assembly.

steps.title: Sew the Wings
steps.content: Layer the wing fabrics with the wadding and stitch around the outer edge, leaving a turning gap. Turn right side out, press carefully and topstitch around the shape. Add decorative stitching lines to create wing details.

tip.text: Do not trim too close to the stitching on curved areas or the seams may weaken.

steps.title: Make the Arms and Legs
steps.content: Pair the arm and leg pieces right sides together and sew around each shape, leaving openings for turning. Turn right side out and lightly stuff before closing the openings.

tip.text: Use a small turning tool to shape narrow limbs neatly.

steps.title: Construct the Body
steps.content: Join the body pieces together, leaving the neck and lower body openings. Insert a craft stick into the neck area for support and firmly stuff the body before closing the openings.

tip.text: Ensure the support stick is fully enclosed and securely stitched inside the body.

steps.title: Attach the Arms
steps.content: Position the arms at the shoulders and stitch them securely to the body. Ensure both arms are aligned evenly before securing permanently.

tip.text: Check arm height from both sides before sewing to avoid uneven placement.

steps.title: Create the Facial Features
steps.content: Draw the face using a removable marker. Embroider the eyes, eyelashes, nose and mouth using embroidery thread. Add subtle cheek colouring with fabric pencils if desired.

tip.text: Complete the face before attaching the hair for easier access.

steps.title: Make the Hair Fringe
steps.content: Thread two needles with cotton yarn and secure strands along the forehead area. Create a satin-stitch style fringe by stitching yarn strands diagonally across the forehead.

tip.text: Work slowly and keep the yarn tension even for a smooth fringe.

steps.title: Add the Main Hair
steps.content: Cut several lengths of yarn, fold them in half and stitch the loops securely to the side seams and back of the head. Continue adding strands until the desired fullness is achieved.

tip.text: Adding too much yarn can make the hairstyle bulky and difficult to manage.

steps.title: Decorate the Hair
steps.content: Add extra yarn strands across the forehead and secure them with a crystal bead to create a decorative hair accessory.

tip.text: Replace beads with embroidery details if the doll is intended for very young children.

steps.title: Make the Fairy Cap
steps.content: Cut the cap pieces from fabric and sew them together. Turn right side out, press and fit over the doll's head, securing with small hand stitches.

tip.text: Clip curved seam allowances before turning for a smoother finish.

steps.title: Sew the Dress Bodice
steps.content: Join the dress front and back pieces at the shoulders. Fold and topstitch the neckline and sleeve edges before sewing the side seams.

tip.text: Finish the neckline before closing the side seams for easier sewing.

steps.title: Finish the Dress
steps.content: Hem the bottom edge of the dress and press thoroughly. Add decorative trim such as ric rac around the neckline or hem if desired.

tip.text: Press after every major seam for a more professional appearance.

steps.title: Attach the Wings
steps.content: Gather the centre of the wings slightly to create shape. Position them at the upper back of the doll and stitch securely in place.

tip.text: Use strong stitches because the wings may be handled frequently during play.

steps.title: Add Dress Fasteners
steps.content: Attach snap fasteners to the back opening of the dress, working around the wing attachment points as needed.

tip.text: Test the dress closure several times before finishing to ensure easy dressing.

steps.title: Complete the Fairy Doll
steps.content: Dress the doll, adjust the hair, wings and clothing, then inspect all seams and embellishments before use.

tip.text: Check that all decorative elements are firmly secured before giving the doll to a child.
