steps.title: Cut the Pattern Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the template. Use the dimensions list and pattern pieces to cut out the jacket fronts, back, sleeves, collar, pockets and faux seam strips from denim or chambray fabric.

tip.text: Mark all pattern pieces before cutting to make assembly easier.

steps.title: Prepare the Front Jacket Pieces
steps.content: Clip into the curved seam allowances around the neckline of the front pieces. Fold the front edges to the wrong side and secure with a glue pen. Create a narrow double hem along each front edge and backstitch in place.

tip.text: Avoid clipping beyond the seam allowance when working around curves.

steps.title: Create Faux Seam Strips
steps.content: Apply glue along the wrong side of each faux seam strip. Fold both long edges into the centre and press flat before securing.

tip.text: Use a pressing tool or fingernail to create crisp folded edges.

steps.title: Attach Faux Seams
steps.content: Position one faux seam strip on each jacket front, aligning the lower edge with the hem. Backstitch down the centre of each strip and trim away any excess fabric.

tip.text: Check both strips are positioned symmetrically before stitching.

steps.title: Prepare the Pockets
steps.content: Turn in the seam allowances around both pocket pieces and secure them with a glue pen. Backstitch across the top edge of each pocket.

tip.text: Press the pocket edges well before attaching them to the jacket.

steps.title: Attach the Pockets
steps.content: Position the pockets on the jacket fronts so that one edge slightly overlaps the faux seam strip. Backstitch around the remaining sides to secure.

tip.text: Ensure both pockets are level and evenly spaced.

steps.title: Join the Back Pieces
steps.content: Place the two back jacket pieces right sides together. Backstitch around the neckline and lower hem edges, clipping curved seam allowances where necessary.

tip.text: Clipping curves helps the neckline sit smoothly when turned.

steps.title: Attach Fronts to Back
steps.content: Place one front jacket piece right sides together with the back section and sew along the shoulder seam. Repeat for the second front piece.

tip.text: Match shoulder edges carefully to keep the jacket balanced.

steps.title: Prepare the Sleeves
steps.content: Mark the centre point of each sleeve by folding it in half widthwise. The sleeve shape allows for small pleats that help fit the armhole smoothly.

tip.text: Use a fabric pen to lightly mark the sleeve centre point.

steps.title: Insert the Sleeves
steps.content: Place each sleeve right sides together with the armhole. Begin sewing from the underarm and work upward, using the centre mark to position any sleeve pleats evenly.

tip.text: Distribute the pleats evenly to avoid puckering at the sleeve cap.

steps.title: Prepare the Collar
steps.content: Clip into the curved seam allowances of the collar pieces. Fold the seam tabs to the wrong side and secure with a glue pen. Backstitch around the outer edges.

tip.text: Do not fold the upper seam allowance because it will be used to attach the collar.

steps.title: Attach the Collar
steps.content: Position one collar piece at the neckline with the right side of the jacket facing the wrong side of the collar. Match seam lines and stitch along the neckline. Fold the collar outward and repeat on the opposite side.

tip.text: Ensure the collar points are aligned evenly on both jacket fronts.

steps.title: Sew the Side Seams
steps.content: Fold the jacket right sides together and stitch from the sleeve cuff down through the underarm and side seam to the hem on both sides.

tip.text: Sew the sleeve and side seam in one continuous line for a cleaner finish.

steps.title: Finish the Sleeves
steps.content: Turn the sleeve cuffs to the wrong side and stitch neatly in place. Press the cuffs flat.

tip.text: A small pressing tool helps achieve crisp miniature hems.

steps.title: Complete the Jacket
steps.content: Turn the jacket right side out, press all seams and check the fit on the doll. Adjust the collar and pockets if necessary before final pressing.

tip.text: Take care when pressing denim fabrics to avoid creating unwanted shine marks.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Cotton fabric fat quarters (beige, white, yellow, dark blue and turquoise)

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Cotton fabric fat quarters: beige, white, yellow, dark blue and turquoise.
Yellow ricrac, 60cm.
Thin ribbon, 45cm.
Wadding.
Round button.
Embroidery thread: pink and navy.
Pink crayon.
Brown yarn.
5mm seam allowance used throughout unless otherwise stated.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Soft Toy Making, Doll Making, Hand Sewing, Machine Sewing, Embroidery, Gathering

steps.title: Prepare the Body Fabrics
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Sew a 9cm x 15cm piece of cream fabric to a 13cm x 15cm piece of yellow fabric and cover the seam with ricrac trim.

tip.text: Press the seam flat before attaching the ricrac for a neat finish.

steps.title: Create the Doll Body
steps.content: Fold the joined fabric in half widthwise with right sides together and pin around the body template. Stitch around the outline, leaving the lower opening unstitched.

tip.text: Do not sew the bottom opening closed, as it is needed for turning and stuffing.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff the Body
steps.content: Trim the seam allowance to approximately 3mm, turn the body right side out and press. Fold the opening inward, stuff firmly with filling and shape the doll evenly.

tip.text: Avoid overstuffing the neck area, which can make attaching clothing difficult.

steps.title: Add Facial Features
steps.content: Colour the cheeks with a pink crayon and embroider the eyes and mouth using embroidery thread.

tip.text: Lightly sketch the facial features first before stitching.

steps.title: Make the Arms and Legs
steps.content: Cut two beige rectangles measuring 7cm x 22cm for the legs and two pieces measuring 7cm x 13cm for the arms. Sew, turn and stuff them in the same way as the body.

tip.text: Use small amounts of stuffing to keep the limbs flexible.

steps.title: Attach the Limbs
steps.content: Insert the legs into the lower body opening and stitch through all layers to secure. Sew the arms neatly to the shoulder areas.

tip.text: Pin the limbs in place before stitching to check symmetry.

steps.title: Create the Skirt
steps.content: Cut a 13cm x 50cm piece of white printed cotton and an 8cm x 50cm piece of yellow fabric. Join them together with a 6mm seam allowance and cover the seam with ricrac.

tip.text: Decorative ricrac helps hide seams while adding detail.

steps.title: Gather the Skirt
steps.content: Fold the fabric strip in half widthwise to create a tube. Sew the edge, fold under 1cm along the top edge and gather with a running stitch.

tip.text: Gather evenly so the skirt sits smoothly around the waist.

steps.title: Attach the Skirt
steps.content: Slip the skirt onto the doll and secure the gathered edge neatly around the waist.

tip.text: Distribute the gathers before permanently stitching the skirt.

steps.title: Make the Sleeves
steps.content: Cut two dark blue rectangles measuring 9cm x 12cm. Sew the long edges, turn right side out and fold so the raw edges align.

tip.text: Press the sleeves before attaching them to achieve crisp edges.

steps.title: Create the Jacket
steps.content: Fold a 14cm x 34cm piece of blue fabric in half widthwise. Pin the jacket template in place, draw around it and cut out. Stitch around the outer edge, trim and turn right side out.

tip.text: Clip curved areas carefully for a smoother finished shape.

steps.title: Attach the Sleeves
steps.content: Slip the sleeves onto the doll's arms with raw edges facing upward and sew them securely to the body.

tip.text: Check that both sleeves sit at the same height before stitching.

steps.title: Finish the Jacket
steps.content: Place the jacket onto the doll. Sew the neckline to the collar area and attach the armholes to the sleeves. Turn back the collar and stitch the marked points to the waistband, leaving a small opening.

tip.text: Keep the collar symmetrical for a balanced appearance.

steps.title: Add the Button Closure
steps.content: Sew a round button to the jacket front to create a decorative fastening.

tip.text: Use matching thread to make the stitching less visible.

steps.title: Create the Hair
steps.content: Wrap brown yarn around a piece of card measuring approximately 30cm x 12cm. Secure the strands, remove them from the card and stitch them to the top of the doll's head. Tie back with ribbon and trim.

tip.text: Secure all yarn strands firmly to prevent them from loosening during play.

steps.title: Make the Heart Accessory
steps.content: Fold a 10cm x 15cm piece of turquoise fabric in half with right sides together. Stitch around the heart template, leaving the turning gap indicated on the pattern.

tip.text: Use short stitches around curved sections for a smoother heart shape.

steps.title: Stuff the Heart
steps.content: Trim the seams, turn the heart right side out and fill lightly with stuffing. Close the opening with small hand stitches.

tip.text: Avoid overstuffing, which can distort the heart shape.

steps.title: Attach the Ribbon Loop
steps.content: Tie a ribbon into a loop and sew it securely to the top of the heart.

tip.text: Double-knot the ribbon before attaching it for extra strength.

steps.title: Position the Heart
steps.content: Slip one of the doll's arms through the ribbon loop and arrange the hands so they appear to hold the heart.

tip.text: Test different arm positions before permanently securing the hands.

steps.title: Final Finishing
steps.content: Inspect all seams, adjust the clothing and hair, trim loose threads and ensure the heart accessory is securely attached.

tip.text: Check that all decorative elements are firmly secured before gifting the doll.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Felted jumper and dark felt fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description: Felted jumper, dark felt fabric (10cm square), safety toy filling, sewing thread, stranded brown embroidery thread, toy safety eyes or buttons, toy joints (20mm, four), sewing needle, tapestry needle.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Soft Toy Making, Hand Sewing, Overstitching, Embroidery, Jointed Toy Construction

steps.title: Prepare the Pattern Pieces
steps.content: Cut all teddy bear pieces according to the cutting guide. From the felted jumper, cut two heads, one head gusset, two ears, four arms, four legs, two tummy pieces and two back pieces. Cut the nose, inner ears, hand soles and foot soles from darker felt.

tip.text: Label mirrored pieces immediately after cutting to avoid confusion during assembly.

steps.title: Join the Head Darts
steps.content: Sew the V-shaped darts on both head pieces. Attach the gusset to one side of the head, matching the nose point and neck markings accurately.

tip.text: Misaligned gusset seams can distort the shape of the teddy's face.

steps.title: Complete the Head
steps.content: Sew the second side of the head to the remaining edge of the gusset, joining the seams neatly from nose to neck.

tip.text: Use small, even stitches around curved sections for a smoother finish.

steps.title: Attach the Ears
steps.content: Sew the inner ear pieces centrally onto the outer ears. Position the completed ears on the head so the outer edges align with the dart seams and stitch securely.

tip.text: Pin both ears in place first and compare their positions before stitching.

steps.title: Create the Face
steps.content: Attach the felt nose to the snout area. Using all six strands of embroidery thread, embroider the nose outline, mouth and facial details.

tip.text: Lightly sketch the mouth placement first to achieve a balanced expression.

steps.title: Insert the Eyes and Stuff the Head
steps.content: Attach safety eyes or sew buttons into place. Once satisfied with the expression, fill the head firmly with toy stuffing.

tip.text: Use embroidered eyes instead of buttons when making toys for very young children.

steps.title: Construct the Arms
steps.content: Sew the hand soles onto the inner arm pieces. Pair the arm sections together and stitch around the outer edges, leaving the opening indicated on the pattern.

tip.text: Remember to leave the turning and stuffing opening before completing the seam.

steps.title: Stuff the Arms
steps.content: Turn the arms right side out and fill them firmly with stuffing while maintaining an even shape.

tip.text: Use small amounts of stuffing at a time to prevent lumps.

steps.title: Construct the Legs
steps.content: Join the leg pieces and sew around the seams, leaving the foot opening accessible. Attach the foot soles by matching the marked front and back points.

tip.text: Clip curved seam allowances carefully to help the foot lie flat.

steps.title: Stuff the Legs
steps.content: Turn the legs right side out and fill approximately the lower two-thirds firmly, ensuring the stuffing reaches the foot area.

tip.text: Push stuffing firmly into the toes and heel area for a realistic shape.

steps.title: Prepare the Body
steps.content: Mark the joint positions on the back pieces and sew the center back seam. Attach the tummy pieces to the body sides, matching all alignment points.

tip.text: Accurate joint placement is essential for balanced movement later.

steps.title: Install the Toy Joints
steps.content: Push the joint stems through the marked holes in the limbs and corresponding holes in the body. Secure them with the supplied washers according to the manufacturer's instructions.

tip.text: Ensure every washer is fully locked before continuing assembly.

steps.title: Finish the Limbs
steps.content: Close the tops of the arms and legs around the joint hardware while adding additional stuffing to create smooth, rounded shapes.

tip.text: Check that each limb rotates freely before closing the seams.

steps.title: Stuff the Body
steps.content: Sew the front tummy seam and gradually fill the body with toy stuffing until it feels firm but slightly squeezable.

tip.text: Uneven stuffing can cause the teddy to lean when sitting.

steps.title: Attach the Head
steps.content: Match the neck markings on the head and body and sew the head securely into place. Add extra stuffing around the neck if necessary.

tip.text: A firmly stuffed neck helps support the weight of the head.

steps.title: Embroider Paw Details
steps.content: Sew three short embroidered lines across the edges of each paw to represent claws and add character.

tip.text: Use matching embroidery thread for a subtle traditional teddy bear look.

steps.title: Felt the Jumper Fabric
steps.content: If preparing your own felted wool fabric, wash a 100% wool or cashmere jumper in a hot wash cycle and dry thoroughly until the fibres shrink and bond together.

tip.text: Only natural wool fibres felt properly; synthetic blends may not produce the desired result.

steps.title: Final Inspection
steps.content: Check all seams, joints and embroidered details. Adjust stuffing if required and ensure all parts are securely attached before displaying or gifting the teddy.

tip.text: Rotate each joint several times to confirm smooth movement and secure installation.

items.name: Boho Rag Doll
items.materialNeeded: Soft washed denim, cotton lawn, floral fabric, gingham fabric, yellow fabric, red spotted fabric, cotton jersey, white felt, assorted ribbons, cord, white buttons, safety toy filling, paper, brown wool.
items.techniques: Soft Toy Making, Doll Construction, Garment Sewing, Hand Stitching, Embroidery, Hair Making

steps.title: Cut the Doll Pieces
steps.content: Using the templates, cut four arm pieces and two pairs of leg pieces from denim. Cut two shoes and two soles from blue felt. From floral fabric, cut one pair of dungaree pieces. From contrast fabric, cut the bib facing, turn-ups and pocket. Cut the T-shirt pieces from white jersey.

tip.text: Transfer all template markings before removing the paper pattern pieces.

steps.title: Sew the Legs
steps.content: Divide the leg pieces into two sets and stitch from the top, around the feet and back to the top using a 3mm seam allowance. Clip around the feet curves, turn right side out and stuff firmly without distorting the shape.

tip.text: Overstuffing the feet can make them bulky and difficult to attach later.

steps.title: Join the Leg Seams
steps.content: Match the back seams to the centre front seams and stitch across the top to complete both legs.

tip.text: Check that both legs are the same length before continuing.

steps.title: Make the Arms
steps.content: Pair the arm pieces and stitch around the edges, clipping into the thumb curves. Turn right side out, stuff lightly and close the openings at the tops of the arms.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to shape the thumb area neatly.

steps.title: Assemble the Body
steps.content: Stitch the centre front and centre back body seams together and sew the two darts at the base of the back body. Match and stitch the shoulder seams and the top of the neck.

tip.text: Misaligned shoulder seams can affect the doll's final posture.

steps.title: Attach Arms and Legs
steps.content: Position the arms at each shoulder on the front body and stitch in place. Attach the legs to the lower edge of the front body, positioning them on the outer edges. Cross the arms over one another and stitch the back body section to the front seams.

tip.text: Ensure the limbs are symmetrical before permanently securing the seams.

steps.title: Stuff the Body
steps.content: Turn the body right side out through the opening at the back. Insert a small strip of card into the neck area and carefully stuff the body, adding more filling to the limbs than the torso.

tip.text: The card insert helps the neck stay upright and prevents drooping.

steps.title: Close the Body Opening
steps.content: Slip stitch the opening at the base of the body closed and cover the entire seam allowance from the tops of the legs.

tip.text: Use matching thread for an almost invisible finish.

steps.title: Create and Attach the Head
steps.content: Mark the facial features onto the head piece. Stitch the two head sections together, leaving the top open. Turn right side out, stuff firmly and close the top opening with a gathering stitch.

tip.text: Uneven stuffing can cause the head to look lopsided.

steps.title: Embroider the Face
steps.content: Embroider the eyes using blue thread and the mouth using pink thread. Add any extra facial details before attaching the head.

tip.text: Lightly sketch the face first with a disappearing marker.

steps.title: Attach the Head
steps.content: Hand stitch the head securely to the front of the neck, allowing the stitching to extend slightly behind the head. Add a few invisible stitches through the neck and chin if needed.

tip.text: A secure neck attachment is essential for durability.

steps.title: Sew the Dungaree Bib
steps.content: Stitch the centre front seam with a 3mm seam allowance and press open. Cut two 12cm ribbon straps and pin them to the bib. Attach the facing, stitch around the top edge, clip curves, turn right side out and press.

tip.text: Pressing after each seam helps the tiny garment sit neatly.

steps.title: Finish the Dungarees
steps.content: Attach the pocket and turn-up cuffs. Stitch the centre back seams and join the inside leg seams. Turn the dungarees right side out.

tip.text: Check the pocket placement before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Make the T-Shirt
steps.content: Cut the T-shirt along the centre back. Attach a folded strip of white jersey around the neckline. Stitch shoulder seams, underarm seams and side seams, then turn right side out and roll up the cuffs. Add a popper to the back neck.

tip.text: A small popper makes dressing and undressing the doll easier.

steps.title: Sew the Shoes
steps.content: Stitch darts into the shoe fronts, sew the back seams and turn right side out. Attach the soles and decorate with gingham ribbon straps secured using small buttons.

tip.text: Replace buttons with embroidered details if the toy is intended for very young children.

steps.title: Create the Hair Base
steps.content: Wind brown wool around a card approximately 35cm wide until the bundle measures about 10cm thick. Remove the wool and stitch through the centre to create a central parting.

tip.text: Keep the strands aligned while removing them from the card.

steps.title: Make the Fringe
steps.content: Wrap yarn around a 6cm card, remove it and stitch through the centre. Sew this smaller section to the front of the head to create the fringe.

tip.text: Trim the fringe gradually rather than cutting it all at once.

steps.title: Attach the Hair
steps.content: Position the larger hair section on the head and hand stitch along the stitched centre line. Secure firmly along the scalp.

tip.text: Loose stitches may allow the hair to shift during play.

steps.title: Create the Pigtails
steps.content: Divide the hair on each side into three sections and braid each into a plait. Secure the ends with ribbons and arrange the braids over the head.

tip.text: Use matching ribbons to complement the doll's outfit.

steps.title: Final Assembly
steps.content: Dress the doll in the T-shirt, dungarees and shoes. Position the plaits neatly and secure them with a few hand stitches if desired.

tip.text: Give the completed doll a final grooming and trim any loose threads before gifting.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Selection of coordinating printed cotton fabrics

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description: Selection of coordinating printed cotton fabrics, embroidery thread, safety toy stuffing, scrap paper, small buttons or embroidered eyes.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Patchwork, Soft Toy Making, Hand Sewing, Machine Sewing, Embroidery

steps.title: Prepare the Patchwork Fabric
steps.content: Cut 81 fabric squares measuring 4.2cm × 4.2cm from coordinating printed cottons. Arrange the squares in an alternating pattern, creating a panel eight squares wide and ten squares long.

tip.text: Lay out all fabric squares before sewing to achieve a balanced colour distribution.

steps.title: Sew the Patchwork Panel
steps.content: Join the squares together using a 5mm seam allowance. Press the seams flat on the reverse side with an iron to reduce bulk.

tip.text: Skipping the pressing step can make the final elephant shape uneven.

steps.title: Create the Elephant Template
steps.content: Trace the elephant pattern onto scrap paper and cut it out. Position the templates on the patchwork fabric so the back legs align along one edge of the panel.

tip.text: Careful template placement helps maximise fabric usage and maintain symmetry.

steps.title: Cut the Body Pieces
steps.content: Pin the template securely and cut out two elephant body pieces. Cut any additional pattern pieces required for the ears and tail.

tip.text: Use sharp fabric scissors to keep the patchwork edges clean.

steps.title: Sew the Elephant Body
steps.content: Place the body pieces right sides together and sew around the outline, leaving an opening along the back for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Do not sew the turning gap closed at this stage.

steps.title: Clip and Turn
steps.content: Clip the curved seam allowances around the trunk, legs and body. Turn the elephant right side out through the opening.

tip.text: Failing to clip tight curves may cause puckering after turning.

steps.title: Stuff the Elephant
steps.content: Fill the elephant evenly with safety toy stuffing, starting with the trunk and legs before filling the body.

tip.text: Use small pieces of stuffing to achieve a smooth, even finish.

steps.title: Close the Back Seam
steps.content: Fold the raw edges of the opening inward and oversew the back seam neatly to close the elephant.

tip.text: A ladder stitch creates an almost invisible seam.

steps.title: Make the Ears
steps.content: Pair the ear pieces right sides together and sew around the edges, leaving a 3cm gap. Turn the ears right side out, flatten them and fold in the raw edges.

tip.text: Uneven ear placement can affect the toy's overall appearance.

steps.title: Attach the Ears
steps.content: Oversew the finished ears securely to each side of the elephant's head.

tip.text: Pin both ears first and compare positions before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Add the Eyes
steps.content: Sew layered buttons above the trunk to create eyes, or embroider the eyes if making the toy for young children.

tip.text: Use embroidered eyes instead of buttons for toys intended for toddlers.

steps.title: Create the Tail
steps.content: Fold a leftover printed fabric square in half and cut a small fringe into one edge. Roll the fabric tightly to form a tassel and secure it with stitches.

tip.text: Keep the fringe cuts evenly spaced for a neat tassel effect.

steps.title: Attach the Tail
steps.content: Sew the tassel securely to the back of the elephant using embroidery thread.

tip.text: Reinforce the tail attachment with several stitches to prevent it from coming loose.

steps.title: Add the Hanging Loop
steps.content: Create a loop using embroidery thread and stitch it to the back of the elephant near the tail area.

tip.text: The loop can be used for hanging the toy as a decoration.

steps.title: Finish the Cord Detail
steps.content: Twist the remaining embroidery thread around the loop to create a decorative cord effect and secure the ends.

tip.text: Matching thread colours help coordinate the tail and hanging loop with the patchwork fabric.

steps.title: Final Inspection
steps.content: Check all seams, ears, eyes and tail attachments. Trim any loose threads and reshape the stuffing if needed.

tip.text: Ensure all embellishments are securely attached before giving the toy to a child.

steps.title: Cut the Tea Cosy Pieces
steps.content: Download the templates. Using the tea cosy template, cut two outer pieces from mustard patterned fabric, noting that the front piece is shorter than the back. Cut two lining pieces and two wadding pieces. Cut a 7cm x 37cm strip from Liberty grass print fabric and back it with iron-on interfacing. Cut all appliqué pieces for the teapot, cup and saucer from assorted fabrics and back them with interfacing.

tip.text: Fuse interfacing before cutting intricate appliqué shapes to prevent fraying.

steps.title: Decorate the Front Panel
steps.content: Back a 14cm circular coaster with interfacing and pin it to the right side of the tea cosy front. Secure with bright pink thread. Arrange and attach the teapot appliqué pieces using pins or fabric glue. Stitch around all shapes using matching thread. Add decorative stitching details and embroider the phrase 'favourite tea' above the cup design.

tip.text: Avoid placing appliqué pieces too close to the curved edge, as they may be caught in later seams.

steps.title: Attach the Bottom Border
steps.content: Fold 38cm of bias binding in half lengthways and stitch along its length. Pin it across the lower edge of the tea cosy front and stitch into place. Fold the lower raw edge under and attach the interfaced grass-print fabric strip, securing it neatly with stitching.

tip.text: Press each fold before stitching to keep the decorative border crisp and even.

steps.title: Quilt the Front Section
steps.content: Layer a lining piece wrong side up, one wadding piece and the completed front panel right side up. Quilt around the appliqué motifs and selected areas of the grass-print fabric. Stitch around the curved outline of the tea cosy and set aside.

tip.text: Use even quilting stitches to prevent puckering between the fabric and wadding layers.

steps.title: Construct the Tea Cosy Back
steps.content: Layer the remaining lining, wadding and back fabric piece. Quilt decorative lines across the patterned fabric and stitch around the curved edge. Place front and back pieces right sides together and insert a mustard grosgrain ribbon loop at the top centre. Stitch around the curved edge, bind the curved seam, turn right side out and finish the lower edge with pink bias binding.

tip.text: Position the hanging loop securely between the layers before stitching the front and back together.

steps.title: Cut the Coaster Pieces
steps.content: Using the coaster template, cut two coaster shapes from blue spot fabric, reversing the template for the back piece. Cut the teapot appliqué pieces from Liberty and mustard fabrics. Back all appliqué components with lightweight interfacing.

tip.text: Remember to reverse the back coaster template so both pieces align correctly.

steps.title: Decorate the Coaster Front
steps.content: Attach the teapot appliqué to the centre of the coaster front, leaving an even border around the edge. Secure with temporary fabric glue and stitch around all appliqué details. Add embroidered decorative details and stitch the word 'tea' using the same method as on the tea cosy.

tip.text: Use contrasting thread colours to highlight the appliqué details.

steps.title: Finish the Coaster
steps.content: Cut a piece of wadding to match the coaster size. Layer the decorated front, the back piece and the wadding underneath. Stitch around the entire coaster with a 5mm seam allowance, leaving a turning gap. Clip the curves, trim excess wadding and turn right side out. Press flat, topstitch 3mm from the edge and quilt around the teapot design to finish.

tip.text: Trim excess wadding before turning to reduce bulk and achieve smoother edges.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Cotton fabric (printed green, plain cream, blue scraps, floral scraps), metallic blue jersey, and green and blue felt

Cotton fabric: printed green (25cm), plain cream (50cm), blue scraps, floral scraps.
Metallic blue jersey.
Green and blue felt.
Fusible interfacing.
Lightweight interfacing.
Embroidery thread.
Red and orange yarn.
Assorted ric rac.
Assorted ribbons.
Assorted sequins.
Small beads.
Four pearl buttons with metal shanks.
Wadding.
Toy stuffing.

Fabric glue.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Toy Making, Appliqué, Embroidery, Stuffing, Hand Sewing

steps.title: Make the Tail Bunting
steps.content: Fuse interfacing to the reverse side of metallic blue fabric. Using the template, cut two tail bunting pieces. Place right sides together and stitch around the edges, leaving a small turning gap. Turn right side out and slipstitch the opening closed. Sew pearl buttons along the lower edge of the bunting.

tip.text: Use a point turner to shape the bunting neatly before topstitching.

steps.title: Construct the Tail
steps.content: Cut two tail pieces from green printed fabric. Attach the finished bunting to the right side of one tail piece. Layer wadding onto the wrong side of the fin section. Stitch the tail pieces together, leaving the top edge open. Turn right side out and add decorative topstitching following the template markings.

tip.text: Do not overstuff the tail area or the fin will lose its flat decorative shape.

steps.title: Create the Mermaid Face
steps.content: Cut two body pieces from cream cotton. Cut eyes and a mouth from felt and attach them using fabric glue. Add a sequin and bead to each eye for decoration. Place the body pieces right sides together and stitch around the outline, leaving the lower edge open.

tip.text: For young children, replace beads and sequins with embroidered details for safety.

steps.title: Join the Body and Tail
steps.content: With the body still inside out, insert the tail so the right sides are facing together and align the waist edges. Stitch around the waist seam. Turn right side out through the opening, stuff firmly and close the remaining gap. Sew and stuff the cream fabric arms separately before attaching them to the body.

tip.text: Stuff the body gradually to achieve a smooth shape without lumps.

steps.title: Make the Bikini Top
steps.content: Cut two bikini pieces from green printed fabric. Stitch them together, leaving a turning gap. Turn right side out and close the opening. Decorate the centre with embroidery, a sequin and a bead. Stitch the bikini top onto the mermaid and tie the straps at the back.

tip.text: Press the bikini top before attaching it to keep the edges crisp.

steps.title: Create the Hair
steps.content: Wrap red and orange yarn around two pieces of card measuring 14cm x 30cm until a thick bundle forms. Cut between the cards and trim one side. Stitch across the centre of the bundle to create a parting. Glue the hair to the head, allow it to dry and then secure it permanently with hand stitching.

tip.text: Secure the yarn firmly with several rows of stitching to prevent strands from loosening during play.

steps.title: Add Decorative Details
steps.content: Cut assorted circles from felt and layer them around the waist seam to resemble scales. Decorate the layers with sequins and beads. Create larger layered felt flowers and attach them with ribbon embellishments. Tie the finished decorative ribbon around the mermaid's neck.

tip.text: Mix different felt sizes and colours to create a more dimensional underwater effect.

steps.title: Sew the Jellyfish Companion
steps.content: Cut two circles measuring 7cm in diameter, one from floral fabric and one from plain blue fabric. Attach ric rac around the edge of the floral circle. Place the circles right sides together and stitch around the edge, leaving an opening for turning.

tip.text: Keep the ric rac facing inward during stitching so it appears correctly after turning.

steps.title: Finish the Jellyfish
steps.content: Turn the jellyfish right side out, add a small amount of stuffing and close the opening. Attach ribbons and ric rac strips underneath as tentacles. Fold a 30cm ribbon in half and sew it to the top of the jellyfish, covering the stitches with a decorative sequin. Tie the finished jellyfish to the mermaid's wrist.

tip.text: Use lightweight stuffing so the jellyfish remains soft and easy to hang from the mermaid's arm.

techPack.description: Stuffing, Sewing, Embroidery, Soft Toy Construction

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Cut one head side, one center head, one front body, one back body, two legs, four arms, and one front and one back body piece from the fur fabric, following the fur direction. Reverse templates where indicated. Cut two middle ear pieces and two middle paw pieces from patterned fabric, then cut two paw pieces from wool felt.

tip.text: Make sure the fur nap runs in the same direction on all body pieces to avoid an uneven finished appearance.

steps.title: Sew the Body and Arms
steps.content: Pin the back body pieces together at the marked center back and stitch. Repeat for the front body pieces. Join the front and back body sections together and sew. Turn right side out and lightly stuff until rounded. Sew the arm sections together, leaving a gap for turning. Turn out, stuff evenly, and close the openings.

tip.text: Stuff the arms firmly at the paws but leave the upper section softer for easier attachment later.

steps.title: Make the Legs and Paws
steps.content: Stitch the leg sections together, leaving a small opening underneath for stuffing. Press the fabric circle into the center of each felt paw and secure. Attach the paw pieces to the leg openings and stitch into place. Turn right side out, stuff firmly, and close the openings.

tip.text: Overstuffing one leg more than the other can cause the bunny to sit unevenly.

steps.title: Construct the Ears
steps.content: Fold a middle ear piece in half and stitch along the dart line. Press the seam open and pin it to a fur ear piece. Place the second ear piece on top with right sides facing and sew together, leaving an opening. Turn right side out, lightly stuff, and close the gap. Repeat for the second ear.

tip.text: Keep the ear stuffing light so the ears remain soft and naturally floppy.

steps.title: Assemble and Stuff the Head
steps.content: Join the two side head sections from nose to neckline, leaving the top open. Pin the center head section into place and stitch carefully. Cut the ear slits where marked, insert the ears, and hand stitch securely. Turn the head right side out and stuff until smoothly rounded. Gather the neck opening with running stitches.

tip.text: Secure the ears firmly with extra stitching because they receive frequent handling.

steps.title: Attach the Limbs
steps.content: Position the arms against the body and use a double thickness of strong thread and a long needle to button-joint them through the body. Repeat the process for the legs so the limbs remain movable.

tip.text: Pull the jointing thread tight enough for stability but not so tight that the limbs cannot move.

steps.title: Attach the Head and Embroider the Face
steps.content: Position the head on the body and secure it with small stitches around the neckline. Using three strands of pink embroidery thread, stitch the nose in satin stitch. Embroider the mouth with black thread and add the eyes. Embroider claw details on the paws with brown thread.

tip.text: Check the eye placement before sewing permanently to keep the bunny’s expression balanced.

steps.title: Create and Attach the Tail
steps.content: Cut a 12cm circle from fur fabric. Sew a running stitch around the edge, pull the thread to form a pouch, and stuff firmly. Pull the stitches tight, tie securely, and stitch the finished tail to the back of the bunny.

tip.text: Add extra stuffing to the tail before closing for a fuller pom-pom effect.

steps.title: Make the Neck Bow
steps.content: Cut a 9cm x 40cm strip of patterned fabric. Fold lengthways with right sides together and stitch along the long edge, leaving a turning gap. Turn right side out, press, close the gap neatly, and tie the strip into a bow around the bunny’s neck.

tip.text: Press the bow fabric well before tying for crisp, professional-looking folds.

steps.title: Cut Out the Farmer Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Trace all pattern pieces onto the reverse side of the fabric and cut out, leaving a 5mm seam allowance. Cut the face, hands and feet from plain fabric. Cut body and arm pieces from patterned fabrics.

tip.text: Transfer all template markings before removing the paper pattern pieces.

steps.title: Sew the Arms and Legs
steps.content: Sew arm and leg pieces right sides together in pairs, leaving turning gaps where indicated. Turn right side out and stuff lightly to maintain flexibility.

tip.text: Overstuffing the limbs can make assembly difficult and reduce poseability.

steps.title: Attach Feet and Arms
steps.content: Sew the feet to the bottom of each leg and position the arms at each side of the body. Match raw edges and stitch securely in place before assembling the body.

tip.text: Double-check arm and leg orientation before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Construct the Body
steps.content: Sew the body pieces together, leaving an opening for turning. Turn right side out, insert stuffing gradually, and shape the body evenly before closing the opening.

tip.text: Use small amounts of stuffing at a time to avoid lumps.

steps.title: Attach the Head
steps.content: Assemble the head pieces according to the markings. Stuff firmly and attach the completed head to the body using a strong backstitch.

tip.text: Secure the neck area thoroughly since it will experience the most stress during play.

steps.title: Embroider the Face
steps.content: Sketch the facial features. Embroider the eyes with satin stitch and add a whipped backstitch mouth. Shape the expression carefully before securing all thread ends.

tip.text: Mark facial features with a washable fabric pen before stitching.

steps.title: Create the Hair
steps.content: Make the hair using short lengths of yarn. Stitch the strands securely around the head and trim evenly to create the desired hairstyle.

tip.text: Uneven yarn lengths can make the hairstyle look untidy.

steps.title: Make the Neckerchief
steps.content: Cut a triangular piece of patterned fabric. Fold and stitch the edges neatly, then tie it around the farmer's neck.

tip.text: Press the neckerchief before tying for a cleaner finish.

steps.title: Sew the Hat Brim
steps.content: Cut two brim pieces and sew them right sides together around the outer edge. Turn right side out, press, and topstitch around the brim.

tip.text: Clip curved seam allowances before turning to help the brim lie flat.

steps.title: Create the Crown
steps.content: Sew the crown pieces together and attach them to the brim. Turn right side out and press carefully to shape the hat.

tip.text: Skipping pressing can leave the hat looking misshapen.

steps.title: Finish the Farmer Hat
steps.content: Topstitch the hat and place it securely on the farmer's head. Add a few hidden stitches to keep it in position.

tip.text: Ensure the hat is attached securely if the toy will be handled frequently.

steps.title: Cut the Dungaree Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the dungaree template. Cut all pieces from patterned fabric, leaving a 5mm seam allowance.

tip.text: Choose lightweight cotton fabrics to reduce bulk around the seams.

steps.title: Sew the Trouser Legs
steps.content: Sew each leg section together along the inner and outer seams. Turn right side out and hem the lower edges.

tip.text: Check that both legs are the same length before hemming.

steps.title: Add the Waistband Elastic
steps.content: Create a casing at the waist and thread elastic through it. Secure the ends and distribute the gathers evenly.

tip.text: Do not twist the elastic inside the casing.

steps.title: Attach the Bib and Straps
steps.content: Prepare the bib and shoulder straps. Stitch them to the front of the dungarees and topstitch neatly around the edges.

tip.text: Press the straps before attaching for crisp, straight edges.

steps.title: Add Functional Pockets
steps.content: Cut pocket rectangles, turn under the seam allowances, and stitch them onto the front of the dungarees.

tip.text: Make the pockets large enough for small toy accessories.

steps.title: Prepare the Bag Panels
steps.content: Cut the bag front, back, lining and appliqué pieces. Fuse the appliqué design onto the front panel and trim neatly.

tip.text: Allow fused appliqué pieces to cool completely before trimming.

steps.title: Decorate the Bag
steps.content: Topstitch around the appliqué details and embroider facial features or decorative accents as desired.

tip.text: Use a shorter stitch length around curves for smoother outlines.

steps.title: Create the Straps
steps.content: Fold the strap pieces lengthwise, sew along the long edges, turn right side out, and press flat.

tip.text: Uneven strap widths can make the finished bag sit crooked.

steps.title: Assemble the Bag
steps.content: Place the outer bag panels right sides together and sew around the sides and base. Repeat with the lining, leaving a turning gap.

tip.text: Do not accidentally sew the lining turning gap closed.

steps.title: Attach Straps and Lining
steps.content: Position the straps between the outer and lining layers. Sew around the top edge and turn the bag through the lining opening.

tip.text: Pin the straps carefully to prevent twisting during assembly.

steps.title: Finish the Bag
steps.content: Close the lining opening, topstitch around the upper edge, and add snap fasteners to complete the closure.

tip.text: Topstitch slowly around the bag opening for a neat professional finish.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Medium-weight cotton, canvas, upholstery fabric, or another durable woven fabric suitable for a stuffed support pillow

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description: Main fabric, polyester fiberfill or pillow stuffing, matching thread, fabric scissors, fabric marking tool, sewing clips or pins, and a hand-sewing needle

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Cutting curved fabric pieces, sewing curved seams, attaching shaped side panels, joining gusset or shaping strips, sewing angled corners, assembling stuffed pillow sections, turning through an opening, stuffing evenly, and closing an opening with a ladder stitch

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Main Body
steps.content: Cut one main body piece measuring 30" × 16". Shape the center section with inward curves to create the areas where the side arm panels will be attached.

tip.text: Mark the inward curves clearly before cutting, and fold the fabric along the centerline if needed to check that both sides are symmetrical.

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Side Panels
steps.content: Cut four fabric pieces for the side arm panels.

tip.text: Keep the side panel pieces organized in matching pairs, especially if the fabric has a directional print or a visible right and wrong side.

steps.title: Cut the Shaping Strips
steps.content: Cut three fabric strips, each 2.5 inches wide. Adjust the length of each strip according to the actual seam length during construction.

tip.text: Cut the strips slightly longer than needed, then trim the excess after sewing to ensure the strip fully covers each curved seam.

steps.title: Sew the Side Panel to the Shaping Strip
steps.content: Place the right sides of one side panel and one shaping strip together. Align the raw edges and sew around the edge, leaving the arm opening unsewn. Trim any excess length from the shaping strip after sewing.

tip.text: Use sewing clips or pins along curved sections to keep the edges aligned and prevent the fabric from shifting while stitching.

steps.title: Sew the Opposite Side Panel
steps.content: Sew the remaining side panel to the opposite side of the shaping strip. Check that both sides are aligned and balanced before stitching.

tip.text: Make sure the second side panel is positioned as a mirror image of the first. Sewing both panels in the same orientation can create a twisted or uneven shape.

steps.title: Sew the Second Side Panel Assembly
steps.content: Repeat the same process to create the second side panel assembly. Make sure both completed side assemblies are constructed in the same way.

tip.text: Place both completed assemblies side by side before continuing to confirm that their shapes and seam placements match.

steps.title: Attach the Side Assemblies to the Main Body
steps.content: Attach one side assembly to one of the inward curved sections of the main body. Sew only one half of the side assembly to the main body, then repeat the same process with the second side assembly on the opposite side.

tip.text: Match the center points and curve endpoints before sewing. If the pieces are misaligned at the beginning, the pillow shape may become uneven or twisted.

steps.title: Attach the Shaping Strip to the Main Body
steps.content: Sew the shaping strip to the back section of the pillow, which is the longer main body section. Leave a distance of 2.5 inches from each side arm section before starting the seam.

tip.text: Mark the 2.5-inch starting and stopping points on both sides before sewing so the shaping strip is positioned evenly.

steps.title: Sew the Corners
steps.content: Starting from the points located 2.5 inches away from the side arm sections, sew diagonally to join the shaping strip and the main body, forming a squared corner.

tip.text: Check that the diagonal seams are symmetrical on both sides before trimming any excess fabric.

steps.title: Sew the Front and Back Body Together
steps.content: Align the front and back body sections along the side seams. Sew around the outer edges to form the complete pillow shape, leaving a 2-inch opening for turning.

tip.text: Do not make the turning opening too small. A narrow opening can make it difficult to turn the shaped pillow right side out and may strain the seams.

steps.title: Turn the Pillow Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the pillow right side out through the opening that was left unsewn.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to gently shape the corners and curved areas without poking through the fabric or stretching the seams.

steps.title: Stuff the Pillow
steps.content: Fill the pillow through the opening with polyester fiberfill or other suitable pillow stuffing. Distribute the stuffing evenly to create a smooth and balanced shape.

tip.text: Add the stuffing gradually in small amounts, working it into the curved sections and corners before filling the center.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Use a ladder stitch to close the opening and complete the pillow.

tip.text: Keep the ladder stitches small and evenly spaced, then gently pull the thread to close the seam neatly and hide the stitches.

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Fabric
steps.content: Prepare one fabric piece measuring 16" x 36.2".

tip.text: Square the fabric before cutting to ensure the finished pillow cover sits evenly and does not twist.

steps.title: Hem the Opening Edges
steps.content: Finish both short edges first. Fold each short edge toward the wrong side twice by 0.4 inch and sew along the folded edge to create a clean hem. Repeat for the opposite side.

tip.text: Uneven double-fold hems can cause the envelope opening to look crooked and affect the fit of the pillow insert.

steps.title: Construct the Pillow Cover
steps.content: Fold the fabric lengthwise so the two hemmed edges overlap by approximately 4 inches, with right sides facing together. Sew along both open side edges.

tip.text: Make sure the overlap remains at least 4 inches wide, otherwise the pillow insert may be visible through the opening.

steps.title: Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the pillow cover right side out through the envelope opening created by the overlapping hemmed edges.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to gently push out the corners for a crisp, square finish.

steps.title: Create the Flange Border
steps.content: Measure and mark a line 1.3 inches from the outer edge of the pillow cover. Topstitch around all four sides following the marked guideline.

tip.text: Use a seam gauge or ruler while marking to keep the flange border evenly spaced around the entire pillow.

steps.title: Insert the Pillow Filling
steps.content: Insert polyester fiberfill or a ready-made pillow insert through the envelope opening. Adjust the filling evenly and complete the project.

tip.text: Unevenly distributed filling can create lumps, so smooth and position the insert carefully before use.

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Fabric
steps.content: Prepare the neck pillow pattern. Trace the pattern onto the fabric and add a 0.4" seam allowance around the entire shape. Cut the fabric along the outer cutting line to create two pillow body pieces.

tip.text: Transfer any center or alignment marks from the pattern before cutting to make matching the curved edges easier during sewing.

steps.title: Sew the Pillow Body
steps.content: Place the two pillow body pieces right sides together. Sew around the entire edge, leaving a 2" opening for turning the pillow right side out.

tip.text: Remember to leave the turning opening unsewn and backstitch at both ends so the seam stays secure during turning.

steps.title: Trim and Clip the Curves
steps.content: Trim away the excess seam allowance and clip the curved edges where needed.

tip.text: Clip close to the curved seams without cutting through the stitching, or the seam may split when the pillow is turned.

steps.title: Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the pillow right side out through the opening.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to gently push out the curved sections without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Stuff the Pillow
steps.content: Fill the pillow with polyester fiberfill through the opening. Spread the stuffing evenly throughout the pillow until it reaches the desired firmness.

tip.text: Add the fiberfill gradually instead of all at once to prevent lumps and achieve an even, comfortable shape.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Use a ladder stitch to close the opening. Tie off the thread securely to complete the neck pillow.

tip.text: Keep the ladder stitches small and evenly spaced so the opening becomes nearly invisible after tightening the thread.

steps.title: Prepare the Cushion Front
steps.content: Cut a 30.79 inches square piece of cream fabric for the cushion front. Cut the border and awning pieces from coordinating fabrics according to the template. Press all fabrics flat before sewing.

tip.text: Accurate cutting and pressing at the start will make appliqué placement much easier later.

steps.title: Construct the Shop Background
steps.content: Sew the decorative border and awning sections onto the cushion front using a 1/4 inch seam allowance. Press seams open and keep the panel square.

tip.text: Failing to press seams after stitching can create bulky areas that affect the appliqué layout.

steps.title: Trace the Appliqué Templates
steps.content: Trace the flower shop components, including the shop sign, door, windows, flower baskets, flower pots and decorative flowers onto the paper side of fusible webbing.

tip.text: Templates will be reversed when fused to fabric, so remember to mirror any directional details.

steps.title: Create the Appliqué Pieces
steps.content: Fuse the traced webbing shapes to the wrong side of the chosen fabrics. Cut out all shapes neatly and remove the paper backing.

tip.text: Use embroidery scissors for cleaner curves around petals, leaves and basket details.

steps.title: Position and Fuse the Design
steps.content: Arrange the shop front elements on the cushion panel, starting with the building structure and finishing with flowers and decorative accents. Fuse all pieces into place.

tip.text: Photograph the arrangement before fusing so you can recreate the layout if pieces shift.

steps.title: Add Free-Motion Embroidery
steps.content: Place stabilizer behind the cushion front and stitch around the appliqué pieces using free-motion embroidery. Add decorative outlines, stems, leaves and floral details.

tip.text: Practice free-motion stitching on fabric scraps first if you are unfamiliar with the technique.

steps.title: Embroider the Shop Details
steps.content: Stitch the shop sign lettering, window details, hanging basket wires and decorative outlines using embroidery thread.

tip.text: Dense stitching in small areas may cause puckering, so keep stitch density consistent.

steps.title: Complete the Floral Embellishments
steps.content: Add the final decorative embroidery to flowers, leaves, flower pots and hanging baskets. Secure all thread ends neatly on the reverse.

tip.text: Vary thread colours slightly to create depth and a hand-illustrated appearance.

steps.title: Assemble the Cushion Cover
steps.content: Place the cushion back and front right sides together. Stitch around the edges, leaving an opening for turning and inserting the cushion pad.

tip.text: Check that all embroidery threads are secured before closing the cushion cover.

steps.title: Finish the Cushion
steps.content: Turn the cover right side out, push out the corners and press. Insert the cushion pad and close the opening with hand stitching or machine stitching.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to create sharp corners without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Prepare and Cut the Pattern Pieces
steps.content: Print and cut the sleep mask and moon pillow templates. Cut all fabric pieces according to the pattern, including front and back sections for both projects. Apply iron-on interfacing to the designated fabric pieces.

tip.text: Label each fabric piece after cutting to avoid confusion when assembling multiple components.

steps.title: Transfer the Facial Features
steps.content: Trace the eye, eyelash, cheek, and decorative details onto the fabric using the template markings. Position the features before stitching.

tip.text: Misaligned facial features are difficult to correct once embroidery has been completed.

steps.title: Create the Applique Details
steps.content: Cut applique shapes for the eyelids, cheeks, moons, and decorative accents from contrasting fabrics. Fuse them to the front pieces using interfacing or applique adhesive.

tip.text: Press applique pieces in place before stitching to prevent shifting during embroidery.

steps.title: Machine Embroider the Features
steps.content: Use machine embroidery or free-motion stitching to sew the eyelashes, eye outlines, stars, moon accents, and decorative sleeping motifs onto the fabric fronts.

tip.text: For very small applique pieces, place tissue paper beneath the fabric while stitching and tear it away after finishing.

steps.title: Assemble the Sleep Mask Front
steps.content: Layer the completed sleep mask front with wadding and the backing fabric. Secure the layers with pins or temporary adhesive spray before stitching.

tip.text: Quilting the layers lightly before assembly helps prevent shifting during use.

steps.title: Insert the Elastic
steps.content: Position the elastic at each side of the sleep mask according to the pattern markings. Secure the ends with reinforcing stitches.

tip.text: Check the elastic is not twisted before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Finish the Sleep Mask Edge
steps.content: Sew around the sleep mask perimeter and apply the bias binding around the curved edge for a neat and durable finish.

tip.text: Stretching the bias binding while sewing can cause the mask edge to ripple.

steps.title: Prepare the Moon Pillow Front
steps.content: Create the moon face applique and embroidered details on the moon front piece. Stitch the eye, eyelash, cheek, stars, and decorative sleeping symbols before construction.

tip.text: Complete all embroidery before assembling the pillow to keep stitching easier and more accurate.

steps.title: Assemble the Moon Pillow
steps.content: Place the moon pillow front and back pieces right sides together. Sew around the curved outer edge, leaving an opening for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Clip the seam allowance around tight curves to help the crescent shape turn smoothly.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff the Pillow
steps.content: Turn the moon pillow right side out and gently push out the crescent points. Fill evenly with fibre filling until the pillow feels soft yet supportive.

tip.text: Overstuffing can distort the crescent shape and make the pillow appear bulky.

steps.title: Close the Pillow Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning gap closed using a ladder stitch or slip stitch. Shape the pillow as you sew to maintain smooth curves.

tip.text: Use matching thread and small stitches for an almost invisible closure.

steps.title: Final Inspection and Finishing
steps.content: Check both the sleep mask and moon pillow for loose threads, uneven stuffing, or embroidery issues. Press lightly if needed and make any final adjustments.

tip.text: Skipping the final shaping step can leave the moon pillow looking asymmetrical.

steps.title: Prepare and Cut the Fabric
steps.content: Print and cut the heart templates. tip.text: Align patterned fabrics carefully before cutting so the design remains balanced across the finished cushion.

steps.title: Create the Cushion Piping Border
steps.content: Join the red cotton strips end to end to create a continuous strip. Fold the strip lengthwise and wrap it around the pom-pom trim, pinning or tacking it securely in place.

tip.text: Joining the strips with mismatched edges can create bulky sections that are difficult to sew smoothly.

steps.title: Sew the Medium Heart Pocket
steps.content: Place the two medium heart pieces right sides together and sew around the curved edge, leaving a small opening for turning. Clip the seam allowance around curves, turn right side out, and press flat.

tip.text: Clip curved seam allowances carefully without cutting into the stitching line.

steps.title: Create the Heart Applique
steps.content: Apply adhesive webbing to the back of the small patterned heart. Position it in the center of the medium heart and fuse it in place with an iron.

tip.text: Check the placement before fusing permanently, as repositioning after pressing is difficult.

steps.title: Attach Decorative Pom-Pom Trim
steps.content: Sew pom-pom trim around the edge of the small applique heart. Stitch close to the trim tape to keep the pom-poms evenly spaced.

tip.text: Allowing the trim to twist while sewing can make the pom-poms sit unevenly.

steps.title: Create the Pocket Front
steps.content: Place one patterned large heart flat with the right side facing up. Position the completed medium heart on top and pin it in place. Stitch around the lower edge only, leaving the upper edge open to form a pocket.

tip.text: Double-check that the pocket opening faces upward before sewing.

steps.title: Attach the Outer Pom-Pom Trim
steps.content: Pin the prepared pom-pom trim around the edge of the large heart front piece with the pom-poms facing inward. Tack the trim in place around the entire perimeter.

tip.text: Keep the trim away from the seam allowance at tight curves to prevent bunching.

steps.title: Assemble the Cushion
steps.content: Place the second large heart piece right sides together with the front piece. Pin securely and sew around the entire cushion edge, leaving an opening large enough for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Forgetting to leave a turning gap will require unpicking stitches later.

steps.title: Clip and Turn the Cushion
steps.content: Trim excess seam allowance and clip all curved sections, especially around the top heart indentation and rounded edges. Turn the cushion right side out through the opening.

tip.text: Do not cut through the stitching when clipping curves or the seam may split after stuffing.

steps.title: Stuff the Cushion
steps.content: Fill the cushion evenly with cushion stuffing, working the filling into the heart curves and corners until the shape is full and symmetrical.

tip.text: Add stuffing gradually and massage it into place to avoid lumps.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning opening closed using a ladder stitch or slip stitch for an invisible finish.

tip.text: Use matching thread and small stitches to make the closure nearly invisible.

steps.title: Final Shaping and Inspection
steps.content: Fluff the cushion, reshape the heart curves, and check that all seams, trim, and pocket edges are secure. Remove loose threads and make any final adjustments.

tip.text: Uneven stuffing distribution can make one side of the heart appear larger than the other.

steps.title: Cut the Cushion and Horse Pieces
steps.content: Print the templates at actual size and cut out all pattern pieces. Cut the square cushion front, cushion backing, horse applique pieces, and horse toy body pieces from the specified fabrics. Transfer all template markings before sewing.

tip.text: Label each applique piece after cutting to avoid confusion when assembling the decorative horse motifs.

steps.title: Prepare the Applique Motifs
steps.content: Apply fusible webbing to the reverse side of the applique fabrics if using. Trace the horse design pieces, cut them out accurately, and position them onto the cushion front following the template layout.

tip.text: Cutting directly on the traced line can make applique pieces too small. Leave the exact shape intact when trimming.

steps.title: Stitch the Horse Applique
steps.content: Secure the applique pieces to the cushion front using a narrow zigzag stitch, satin stitch, or decorative machine embroidery stitch. Work slowly around curves and points for a neat finish.

tip.text: Pulling the fabric while stitching curves can distort the applique shape and cause puckering.

steps.title: Add Ribbon and Embroidered Details
steps.content: Attach decorative ribbon trims to the horse design and embellish with embroidery details such as hearts, borders, and traditional Scandinavian-inspired motifs. Stitch all embellishments securely.

tip.text: Use an embroidery hoop when adding decorative stitching to keep the fabric smooth and prevent wrinkles.

steps.title: Construct the Square Cushion Front
steps.content: Complete all applique and embroidery work on the cushion front. Press the panel carefully from the reverse side using a pressing cloth to protect decorative stitching.

tip.text: Pressing directly onto applique stitching can flatten decorative details and damage delicate trims.

steps.title: Assemble the Square Cushion
steps.content: Place the cushion front and backing right sides together. Stitch around the perimeter, leaving an opening for turning. Clip corners, turn right side out, and press carefully.

tip.text: Failing to clip the corners before turning will result in bulky, rounded cushion corners.

steps.title: Insert Cushion Pad and Close Opening
steps.content: Insert the cushion pad through the opening. Adjust the corners and edges until evenly filled. Hand sew the opening closed using an invisible ladder stitch.

tip.text: Push the cushion pad firmly into each corner before closing the opening for a crisp professional finish.

steps.title: Sew the Horse Ornament Front and Back
steps.content: Place the horse body pieces right sides together and stitch around the shape, leaving a turning gap. Clip curved seam allowances and trim excess fabric around tight corners.

tip.text: Do not clip through the stitching line when trimming curves, as this can weaken the seams.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff the Horse
steps.content: Turn the horse right side out through the opening. Carefully shape the legs, ears, and curves before stuffing evenly with toy filling until firm but not overfilled.

tip.text: Overstuffing can distort the horse shape and place unnecessary stress on the seams.

steps.title: Finish the Horse Cushion
steps.content: Close the turning opening with hand stitching. Add any final embroidery details, decorative trims, or embellishments. Press lightly and inspect all seams before displaying.

tip.text: Use matching thread for the closing stitches so the seam becomes virtually invisible.

tip.text: Skipping the basting step can cause trims to shift while sewing the body seams.

steps.title: Sew the Seahorse Body
steps.content: Place the two body pieces right sides together. Stitch around the entire seahorse shape, leaving the marked opening for turning and stuffing. Sew carefully around the curved head and curled tail sections.

tip.text: Use a shorter stitch length around tight curves to prevent jagged seam lines and improve durability.

steps.title: Clip Curves and Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Trim seam allowances and clip into curved areas around the neck, head, and tail. Turn the seahorse right side out through the opening and gently shape all curves using a blunt turning tool.

tip.text: Do not cut through the stitching when clipping curves, as this can cause seam failure after stuffing.

steps.title: Add Facial Details
steps.content: Create the eye using embroidery, a bead, or a button depending on the intended user. Stitch securely and add any additional decorative details before stuffing.

steps.title: Stuff the Seahorse
steps.content: Fill the seahorse evenly with toy stuffing, starting with the nose and working toward the body and tail. Shape the curved tail carefully as you stuff.

tip.text: Add stuffing in small amounts rather than large handfuls to achieve a smooth, even shape without lumps.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand stitch the turning opening closed using a ladder stitch or slip stitch. Ensure the seam is neat and nearly invisible from the outside.

tip.text: Use thread that matches the fabric exactly to hide the closing stitches.

steps.title: Create the Cushion Cover
steps.content: For the cushion version, sew the front and back cushion panels together, inserting any gusset sections as indicated. Leave an opening for inserting the cushion pad.

steps.title: Insert Cushion Pad and Finish

tip.text: Failing to square the panel before continuing can result in uneven cushion seams later.

steps.title: Prepare Butterfly Applique Pieces
steps.content: Trace the butterfly templates onto fusible applique web and fuse them to selected patterned fabrics. Cut out the butterfly shapes accurately and remove the backing paper.

tip.text: Use contrasting fabric prints for different butterflies to create more visual interest on the cushion.

steps.title: Apply the Butterfly Decorations
steps.content: Arrange the butterfly appliques across the cushion front and fuse them into place. Machine stitch around each butterfly using a small zigzag stitch or decorative applique stitch to secure the raw edges.

tip.text: Do not stretch the fabric while stitching around curves, or the butterflies may pucker.

steps.title: Construct the Cushion Cover
steps.content: Place the cushion front and back pieces right sides together. Sew around all four edges, leaving an opening large enough for the cushion pad. Clip corners, turn right side out, and press.

steps.title: Insert Cushion Pad and Finish
steps.content: Insert the cushion pad through the opening and close the gap using a ladder stitch or a neat machine seam.

steps.title: Cut Butterfly Body and Wings

steps.title: Assemble the Butterfly Wings
steps.content: Sew the wing sections together following the template arrangement. Press all seams flat and trim the completed wings to match the template shape.

steps.title: Sew and Stuff the Butterfly Body
steps.content: Place the butterfly body pieces right sides together and stitch around the edge, leaving a turning opening. Turn right side out, stuff firmly with fiber filling, and close the opening by hand.

steps.title: Attach the Wings

steps.title: Add Facial Details

steps.title: Complete the Butterfly Decoration

steps.content: Transfer all inner petal shapes that will be removed to create the decorative cutwork effect. Check that all petals are evenly spaced before cutting.

tip.text: Skipping a final layout check can result in uneven petal spacing and an unbalanced flower design.

steps.title: Cut Out the Petal Openings
steps.content: Carefully cut along the marked inner petal lines using sharp embroidery scissors. Remove each petal section while keeping the outer flower shape intact.

tip.text: Avoid pulling or stretching the felt while cutting, as this can distort the finished flower shape.

steps.title: Secure the Raw Edges
steps.content: Using matching thread, work an oversewing stitch around each cut edge to strengthen the openings and create a neat decorative finish.

tip.text: Keep your stitches evenly spaced to achieve a professional-looking cutwork finish.

steps.title: Prepare the Contrast Layer
steps.content: Cut a cotton backing square slightly larger than the felt front. Place the cotton behind the cutwork panel so the contrasting colour shows through the flower openings.

tip.text: Bright contrasting colours create a stronger visual effect through the cutwork petals.

steps.title: Attach the Decorative Front
steps.content: Pin the felt and cotton layers together. Stitch around the outer flower design and around the panel edges to secure both layers permanently.

tip.text: Insufficient pinning may allow the cotton backing to shift and become misaligned.

steps.title: Prepare the Cushion Back
steps.content: Cut a matching back panel to the same size as the completed front. Press all pieces flat and trim any uneven edges.

tip.text: Square and even panels make final assembly much easier and improve the finished appearance.

steps.title: Assemble the Cushion Cover

tip.text: Use a blunt point turner rather than scissors to avoid accidentally piercing the fabric.

steps.title: Close and Finish
steps.content: Hand stitch the opening closed using an invisible ladder stitch. Smooth the cushion and shape the flower design so the contrast fabric is evenly visible through the cutwork openings.

tip.text: A ladder stitch creates a nearly invisible closure and gives the cushion a clean professional finish.

tip.text: Ensure all buttons are sewn securely, especially if the cushion may be displayed where children can access it.

steps.title: Assemble the Cushion Cover
steps.content: Place the front and back panels right sides together. Pin and machine stitch around the perimeter using a 1.1.97 inches seam allowance. Trim seam allowances where necessary and turn the cover right side out through the zip opening.

tip.text: Clip the corners diagonally before turning to achieve crisp, professional-looking corners.

steps.title: Insert the Cushion Pad
steps.content: Insert the cushion pad through the concealed zip opening. Smooth the corners and check that all embellishments are securely attached. Close the zip to complete the project.

tip.text: Overstuffing the cushion can distort the applique design and make the cover difficult to zip closed.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Free-motion embroidery, Machine sewing, Hand tacking, Seam pressing, Slip stitch, Decorative trim application, Button sewing, Turning and stuffing cushion covers

steps.title: Prepare the Front Panel
steps.content: Cut the green floral fabric, beige square print fabric, and cream felt according to the template measurements. Stitch the floral and beige fabrics together with right sides facing and press the seam open. Attach the cream felt section and press flat.

tip.text: Press every seam as you sew to keep the finished cushion front smooth and professional.

steps.title: Transfer the Embroidery Design
steps.content: Print the embroidery template and trace the floral design onto tissue paper. Position the tissue over the cream felt section and secure it with large hand tacking stitches. Place tearaway stabiliser behind the fabric.

tip.text: Skipping the stabiliser can cause puckering and uneven embroidery stitches.

steps.title: Stitch the Floral Embroidery
steps.content: Using free-motion machine embroidery, stitch over the traced lines twice. Add darker thread shades where desired to create depth and shadow. Carefully remove the tissue paper and tearaway stabiliser once the embroidery is complete.

tip.text: Remove tissue paper slowly to avoid pulling or damaging the embroidery stitches.

steps.title: Press the Embroidered Panel
steps.content: Press the embroidered section from the reverse side of the fabric to protect the stitched design and flatten the panel.

tip.text: Use a pressing cloth to prevent flattening the embroidered texture.

steps.title: Create the Cushion Back
steps.content: Cut the backing fabric to match the finished front panel. Place the front and back pieces right sides together and pin securely around the edges.

tip.text: Misaligned edges can make the finished cushion appear uneven.

steps.title: Sew the Cushion Cover
steps.content: Machine stitch around the perimeter using a 3/8 inch seam allowance, leaving an opening for turning and inserting the cushion pad.

tip.text: Do not sew the turning opening closed, or you will not be able to insert the cushion pad.

steps.title: Trim and Turn
steps.content: Trim excess fabric from the corners to reduce bulk. Turn the cushion cover right side out and carefully shape the corners.

tip.text: Use a blunt point turner rather than scissors to avoid piercing the fabric.

steps.title: Insert the Cushion Pad
steps.content: Insert the appropriate cushion pad into the cover and distribute the filling evenly so the cushion keeps its shape.

tip.text: Fluff the cushion pad before inserting it for a fuller finish.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand sew the opening closed using an invisible slip stitch to create a neat finish.

tip.text: Large slip stitches may be visible from the outside and weaken the seam.

steps.title: Add Lace and Ribbon Trim
steps.content: For the square cushion variation, stitch lace across the front of the cushion and sew the tape measure ribbon beneath it. Press lightly from the reverse side.

tip.text: Pin trims in place before sewing to ensure they remain straight.

steps.title: Attach Decorative Buttons
steps.content: Hand sew three shell buttons evenly across the lower section of the cushion front to complete the design.

tip.text: Decorative buttons may present a choking hazard if the cushion is intended for young children.

steps.title: Cut the Cushion Front and Appliqué Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Cut a 44.1.97 inches square from plain linen fabric for the cushion front. Using the templates, cut the tree trunk, branches, clouds, leaves and decorative shapes from assorted printed fabrics. Apply fusible interfacing to the back of all appliqué pieces.

tip.text: Apply interfacing before cutting detailed shapes to prevent distortion and fraying.

steps.title: Arrange and Stitch the Appliqué Design
steps.content: Trace the layout onto tissue paper. Position the tree, clouds and decorative pieces on the cushion front, leaving space for the lettering. Pin everything in place and machine stitch around each shape. Press from the reverse side when finished.

tip.text: Do not place appliqué pieces inside the seam allowance area or they may be partially hidden after assembly.

steps.title: Add the Fabric Lettering
steps.content: Trace the lettering guide onto tissue paper. Position the fabric letters on the cushion front and stitch around each letter twice. Carefully remove the tissue paper and press the cushion front from the reverse side.

tip.text: Pull tissue paper away slowly to avoid stretching or breaking decorative stitches.

steps.title: Create Decorative Embellishments
steps.content: Stitch decorative birds and details around the appliqué scene. Add any extra decorative stitching shown in the design. Press the completed front panel flat.

tip.text: Use contrasting thread colours to make decorative stitching stand out.

steps.title: Add the Side Border Strips
steps.content: Cut two mustard cotton strips measuring approximately 2.1.97 inches x 44.1.97 inches. Stitch one strip to each side of the completed front panel using a narrow seam allowance. Trim excess fabric and press the seams open.

tip.text: Uneven seam allowances can cause the cushion front to become slightly skewed.

steps.title: Prepare the Envelope Back Panels
steps.content: Cut the required mustard cotton and floral print fabric pieces for the cushion back. Hem the overlapping edges and attach the coordinating ribbon as shown. Press all folds and seams flat.

tip.text: Press each hem before stitching to achieve cleaner and more accurate edges.

steps.title: Assemble the Cushion Cover
steps.content: Place the cushion front right side up. Layer the back panels right side down, overlapping them to create the envelope opening. Align all raw edges, pin securely and stitch around the entire cushion using a 5mm seam allowance.

tip.text: Ensure the envelope overlap faces inward before sewing or the opening will be on the outside.

steps.title: Turn and Finish the Cushion
steps.content: Clip the corners to reduce bulk and turn the cushion cover right side out through the envelope opening. Carefully push out the corners, press the cover flat and insert the cushion pad. Tie the ribbon into a decorative bow if desired.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to shape corners neatly without damaging the fabric.
