Fabric, 3.5m (59.06 inches wide).
Fusible interfacing, 19.69 inches.
Small buttons, 5.
Elastic.
Press stud.
Matching thread.
1.1.97 inches seam allowance used throughout, unless otherwise stated.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Facings, Buttonholes, Elastic Casing, In-Seam Pockets, Garment Construction

steps.title: Prepare the Facings and Back
steps.content: Download and print the template. Apply fusible interfacing to the front facing and back neck facing. Sew the facings together at the shoulder seams and press open. Finish the outer edge of the facing. Mark the elastic casing placement on the garment pieces. Sew the centre-back seam, then trim, neaten and press.

tip.text: Transfer all pattern markings before removing the paper pattern to ensure accurate placement of the casing and closures.

steps.title: Join the Front and Back Sections
steps.content: Sew the centre-front seam to the marked dot with right sides together. Trim and neaten the seam allowance, then press. Join the front and back sections at the shoulder seams and press the seams flat.

tip.text: Sewing beyond the marked dot can distort the V-neck opening and affect the fit of the facing.

steps.title: Attach the Neck Facing
steps.content: Pin the facing to the neckline, matching the centre back and all notches. Stitch around the neckline, ending at the marked dot. Clip curves and trim seam allowances. Understitch the facing and press it to the inside of the garment. Secure the front facing neatly over the centre-front seam.

tip.text: Clip carefully into curved seam allowances without cutting through the stitching line.

steps.title: Create the Front Closure and Attach Pockets
steps.content: Mark and sew the buttonholes on the front facing. Attach the buttons and check the closure alignment. Stitch the side seams and attach the pocket bags. Press the pocket seams away from the garment and secure the pocket edges in place.

tip.text: Test the button placement before sewing permanently to ensure the front edges overlap evenly.

steps.title: Finish the Side Seams and Legs
steps.content: Continue stitching from the underarm to the pocket opening and down to the hem. Stitch around each pocket bag and press the pockets towards the front. Match the notches and sew the inside leg seams. Trim, neaten and press all seams.

tip.text: Avoid catching the pocket bags in the side seam beyond the marked stitching points.

steps.title: Insert the Elastic Waist Casing
steps.content: Fold and press the casing. Stitch it in place beneath the finished front edge. Measure the required elastic length, thread it through the casing and secure the ends. Tuck the elastic ends neatly beneath the facing and stitch securely.

tip.text: Try on the garment before securing the elastic permanently to achieve the most comfortable fit.

steps.title: Complete the Garment
steps.content: Attach a press stud inside the facing where the elastic and facing meet to prevent strain on the opening. Finish the sleeve edges with a narrow hem. Check the trouser length, turn up the hems and stitch in place. Give the jumpsuit a final press.

tip.text: Always test the hem length while wearing the intended footwear before stitching permanently.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Faux suede fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Faux suede fabric, 1.7m (59.06 inches wide).
Matching thread.
1.1.97 inches seam allowance used throughout unless otherwise stated.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Waterfall Front Construction, Sleeve Insertion, Understitching, Gathering, Hemming

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Main Pieces
steps.content: Cut out all pattern pieces according to the cutting guide. Neaten the centre-front edges, upper front edges and side edges. With right sides together, sew the front and back pieces together at the shoulder seams. Press the seams open, ensuring the extra length on the back shoulder seam is positioned towards the neckline.

tip.text: Lay all pattern pieces in the same nap direction when working with faux suede to avoid colour shading differences.

steps.title: Attach the Back Neck Facing
steps.content: With right sides together, pin and sew the back neck facing to the back neckline. Clip into the neckline curve where required and understitch the facing to keep it rolled to the inside. Fold the facing into position and stitch along the shoulder seam lines to secure it neatly.

tip.text: Skipping understitching may cause the facing to roll outward and become visible from the right side.

steps.title: Construct and Insert the Sleeves
steps.content: Sew the underarm seams of the sleeves with right sides together and neaten the raw edges. Stitch two rows of gathering stitches around each sleeve head. Match the sleeve notches with the armhole markings and gently ease the sleeve into the armhole before stitching. Neaten the armhole seam allowances and press.

tip.text: Avoid pulling the gathering threads too tightly or puckers may form around the sleeve cap.

steps.title: Finish the Side Seams
steps.content: With right sides together, match the underarm seams and side seams of the jacket. Stitch continuously from the sleeve cuff to the lower hem. Neaten the seam allowances and press them towards the back of the garment.

tip.text: Pin the underarm seam intersection first to keep all seams aligned accurately.

steps.title: Create the Waterfall Front
steps.content: Carefully press the waterfall front edges into their natural drape. Check that both front panels fall evenly and mirror each other. Adjust and press again if necessary before hemming.

tip.text: Uneven pressing can cause one waterfall front edge to hang longer than the other.

steps.title: Hem the Sleeves
steps.content: Neaten the sleeve cuff edges. Turn up a 2.1.97 inches hem allowance, press firmly and stitch in place. Repeat for the second sleeve, ensuring both cuffs are identical in depth.

tip.text: Use plenty of steam and a pressing cloth when hemming faux suede for a crisp finish.

steps.title: Hem the Jacket
steps.content: Neaten the lower edge of the jacket. Turn up a 2.1.97 inches hem along the entire lower edge and press carefully. Stitch the hem evenly, maintaining a consistent distance from the folded edge.

tip.text: Check the garment length on a dress form or while wearing it before permanently stitching the hem.

steps.title: Final Press and Finish
steps.content: Give the completed jacket a final press, shaping the waterfall front and smoothing all seams. Remove any visible markings and inspect the garment for loose threads before wearing.

tip.text: Allow the jacket to cool completely after pressing so the waterfall folds keep their shape.

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Garment Construction, Collar Attachment, Set-in Sleeves, Hood Construction, Stud Fastener Installation, Hem Finishing

steps.title: Prepare the Coat and Collar
steps.content: Download and print the pattern. Cut out all pieces following the cutting guide. With right sides together, sew the shoulder seams of the coat. Sew the collar pieces together, trim the seam allowances at the corners, turn right side out and press carefully using a pressing cloth.

tip.text: Use a pressing cloth when working with laminate fabric to avoid damaging the waterproof coating.

steps.title: Attach the Collar
steps.content: Match the centre back neck of the coat with the centre back of the collar and pin in place. Continue pinning around the neckline, clipping into the seam allowance where needed to help the collar curve smoothly. Stitch the collar to the neckline and edge-stitch neatly along the collar edge.

tip.text: Failing to clip curved seam allowances can cause the collar to pull and sit unevenly.

steps.title: Sew the Front Facings
steps.content: Place the front facings and coat fronts right sides together. Pin around the neckline, front edges and facing base. Stitch the seams, trim bulk from the corners, turn the facings to the inside and press flat.

tip.text: Reducing seam bulk before turning helps achieve crisp edges and a professional finish.

steps.title: Construct the Body and Sleeves
steps.content: Sew the front and back side seams together and press them open. Create gathering stitches across the sleeve caps between the notches. Sew the sleeve seams to form tubes and prepare them for insertion into the armholes.

tip.text: Do not pull the gathering threads too tightly or the sleeve cap shape may become distorted.

steps.title: Insert Sleeves and Finish Hems
steps.content: Ease the sleeve caps into the armholes, matching all notches carefully. Stitch the sleeves in place and press the seams. Fold and secure the sleeve hems and coat hem using hemming web, ensuring both hems are even all the way around.

tip.text: Mixing up the front and back sleeve notches can result in twisted sleeves.

steps.title: Construct the Hood
steps.content: Sew the hood outer pieces together along the curved edge. Repeat for the lining, leaving a turning gap. Place hood and lining right sides together, stitch around the front edge, clip curves and turn right side out through the gap. Press and close the opening with hand stitching.

tip.text: Remember to leave the turning gap in the lining or the hood cannot be turned right side out.

steps.title: Install Stud Fasteners
steps.content: Attach four stud fasteners down the front opening of the coat. Install three additional studs beneath the collar and at the corresponding points on the hood to create the detachable fastening system.

tip.text: Test the hood alignment with pins before fixing the studs permanently.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Garment Construction, Collar Assembly, Bias Binding Application, Set-in Sleeves, Buttonholes, Button Sewing

steps.title: Construct the Front and Collar
steps.content: Download and print the pattern, then cut all pieces according to the cutting guide. Place the front jacket pieces on top of one another with right sides facing. Match the centre-back collar and stitch the seams together. Press the seam allowances open.

tip.text: Press seam allowances after every seam to achieve a crisp, professional finish.

steps.title: Attach the Back Section
steps.content: Place the back piece onto the front section with right sides together and align the shoulder seams. Clip to the marked dot on the front piece to release the neckline. Match the shoulders and neckline, aligning the centre-back neckline with the back collar seam, then sew in one continuous line.

tip.text: Be careful not to clip beyond the marked dot, as this may weaken the neckline seam.

steps.title: Finish the Neckline and Side Seams
steps.content: Open and press the seam allowance across the back neckline. Apply bias binding over the seam allowance, turning in both ends before edge-stitching in place. Match and sew the side seams of the front and back pieces, then press the seams open.

tip.text: Twisting the bias binding before stitching can create puckers along the neckline.

steps.title: Prepare and Insert the Sleeves
steps.content: Increase the stitch length and sew gathering stitches around each sleeve head between the front and back notches. Sew the underarm sleeve seams with right sides together and press open. Gently pull the gathering threads to shape the sleeve cap, then match the notches and pin the sleeves into the armholes before stitching in place.

tip.text: Pull gathering threads gradually from both ends to distribute fullness evenly around the sleeve cap.

steps.title: Add Buttonholes and Buttons
steps.content: Create three buttonholes at the marked positions on the front jacket piece. Hand-sew the corresponding buttons onto the opposite front edge, ensuring they align correctly with the buttonholes.

tip.text: Test button placement before sewing permanently to ensure the asymmetrical front closes correctly.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Fabric, 2.1m (59.06 inches wide).
Zip, 7.87 inches.
Hook and bar fastening.
Matching thread.
1.1.97 inches seam allowance used throughout unless otherwise stated.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Zip Insertion, Pleat Construction, Waistband Sewing, Hemming

steps.title: Prepare the Trouser Pieces
steps.content: Download and cut out the pattern pieces. Sew the darts into the back trouser panels, then stitch the centre-back seam and neaten the raw edges. Join the lower front sections beneath the zip opening following the pattern markings and press the seams flat.

tip.text: Press each dart toward the centre back to achieve a smooth fit through the waist.

steps.title: Insert the First Side of the Zip
steps.content: Position the zip beneath the folded right-front edge, ensuring the top of the zip sits approximately 2.1.97 inches below the waistband seam. Using a zipper foot, stitch close to the folded edge to secure the zip neatly in place.

tip.text: Check the alignment carefully before stitching, as repositioning a zip can leave visible needle marks.

steps.title: Attach the Second Side of the Zip
steps.content: Secure the opposite zip tape to the facing on the inside of the trousers. Stitch close to the zip teeth, then fold the facing into position and topstitch neatly. Shape the lower end of the zip opening according to the pattern and form the front pleats.

tip.text: Stitching too close to the zipper teeth may prevent the zip from opening and closing smoothly.

steps.title: Sew the Trouser Legs
steps.content: With right sides together, sew the side seams and inside leg seams. Neaten the raw edges and press the seams toward the back. Check that both legs match evenly before proceeding.

tip.text: Match seam intersections carefully at the crotch area to improve the overall fit.

steps.title: Construct the Waistband
steps.content: Join the short ends of the waistband, trim the seam allowances and press. Fold the waistband lengthways and create the inverted pleats marked on the pattern. Stitch across the pleat bases to secure the paperbag effect.

tip.text: Use steam when pressing the pleats to create crisp, long-lasting folds.

steps.title: Make and Attach Belt Carriers
steps.content: Fold and stitch the belt-carrier strip, then turn and press it. Cut into individual carriers and position them at the centre back, side seams and pleat locations. Stitch securely to the waistband edge.

tip.text: Unevenly spaced belt carriers can make the finished belt sit crookedly.

steps.title: Attach the Waistband
steps.content: Pin the waistband to the upper edge of the trousers, matching all pleats and seam lines. Stitch in place and press the seam allowance downward toward the trousers.

tip.text: Basting the waistband before machine stitching helps prevent shifting layers.

steps.title: Finish the Trousers
steps.content: Neaten the leg hems and turn up a 2.1.97 inches hem allowance. Stitch the hems in place. Create the matching fabric tie by folding and stitching all edges neatly. Finish by attaching the hook-and-bar fastening to the waistband.

tip.text: Try on the trousers before hemming to ensure the finished length is correct.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Dart Sewing, Collar Construction, Set-in Sleeves, Interfacing Application, Buttonholes

steps.title: Prepare the Jacket Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the pattern, then cut out all fabric pieces according to the cutting guide. Transfer all markings. Sew the darts in the front jacket pieces from the wide end to the point and press them toward the centre. Finish the shoulder and side edges using an overlocker or zigzag stitch.

tip.text: Press darts over a tailor's ham to maintain the garment's curved shaping.

steps.title: Construct the Collar
steps.content: Apply fusible interfacing to the front facings and one collar piece. Place the collar pieces right sides together and stitch around the outer edges, leaving the neckline edge open. Trim the seam allowances, turn right side out and press carefully.

tip.text: Bulky seam allowances left in the collar corners can prevent sharp points from forming.

steps.title: Join the Shoulder Seams
steps.content: Place the front and back jacket pieces right sides together and stitch the shoulder seams. Press the seam allowances open. Position the completed collar centrally along the neckline, matching the centre back and shoulder notches, then stitch in place.

tip.text: Pin the collar thoroughly before stitching to prevent stretching along the neckline.

steps.title: Attach the Facings
steps.content: Join the front facings to the back neck facing at the shoulder seams and press open. Place the facing onto the jacket, right sides together, enclosing the collar. Stitch around the neckline, front opening and lower front edges. Sew the side seams and press all seams open.

tip.text: Clip curved seam allowances before turning to help the facing lie flat.

steps.title: Prepare the Sleeves
steps.content: Finish the long sleeve edges. Sew a gathering stitch between the front and back sleeve notches along the sleeve cap. Stitch the underarm seams with right sides together, press the seams open, then turn the sleeves right side out.

tip.text: Use a longer stitch length for gathering so adjustments are easier when fitting the sleeve.

steps.title: Set the Sleeves
steps.content: Pull the gathering threads gently to shape the sleeve cap. Match the sleeve notches to the armhole, align the underarm seams, then pin and stitch the sleeves into the armholes. Finish the seam allowances and press toward the sleeve.

tip.text: Uneven gathering can create puckers around the sleeve head.

steps.title: Finish the Jacket
steps.content: Turn up and press a 1.18 inches hem at the sleeve cuffs and lower edge of the jacket. Hand-stitch the hems in place. Create three buttonholes on the right front and sew three matching buttons onto the left front. Position and stitch the shoulder pads in place, securing the facing shoulder seams to the pads to prevent the facings from rolling outward.

tip.text: Test buttonhole settings on a fabric scrap before sewing on the finished jacket.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Knitted fabric and jersey fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Knitted fabric, 1.7m (1.5m wide).
Jersey fabric, 11.81 inches.
Grosgrain ribbon, 6.2m.
Matching thread.
Pins or clips.
1.1.97 inches seam allowance used throughout unless otherwise stated.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Sewing Knits, Neckband Construction, Edge Binding, Mitred Corners

steps.title: Prepare the Poncho and Neckband
steps.content: Cut out all pieces according to the cutting guide. Fold the poncho in half lengthwise and locate the neckline markings. Sew the two short ends of the neckband together with right sides facing to form a loop. Turn the neckband right side out and pin the seam to the centre-back neckline of the poncho. Match the centre-front of the neckband to the centre-front neckline and pin the remaining section evenly before stitching in place.

tip.text: Use clips instead of pins on knitted fabrics to avoid stretching or leaving visible holes.

steps.title: Finish the Neckline
steps.content: Fold one long edge of the neckband under by 1.1.97 inches and press. Position the folded edge over the neckline seam allowance, enclosing the raw edges inside the band. Slip stitch the folded edge neatly to the neckline to create a clean finish.

tip.text: Avoid stretching the neckband while sewing or the neckline may become distorted.

steps.title: Attach the Grosgrain Ribbon
steps.content: Pin the grosgrain ribbon along the right side of all four outer edges of the poncho, covering approximately 0.39 inches of the fabric edge. Edge stitch the ribbon in place, sewing carefully to each corner. Leave the needle down at every corner, lift the presser foot, rotate the poncho and continue stitching along the next edge.

tip.text: Press the ribbon before attaching it to help it lie flat and achieve a more professional finish.

steps.title: Create Mitred Corners and Finish
steps.content: Trim excess fabric bulk from the corners. Fold the ribbon around to the wrong side of the poncho and form neat mitred corners. Pin securely and edge stitch along the ribbon, enclosing all raw edges inside the binding. Give the poncho a final press to complete the reversible finish.

tip.text: Trim corner bulk carefully to avoid cutting into the stitching line.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Pocket Construction, Sleeve Setting, Gathering, Ribbing Application, Zip Insertion, Jacket Lining

steps.title: Prepare the Pocket Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the template. Cut all fabric and lining pieces according to the cutting guide. Position the pocket pieces along the side edges of both the front and back jacket pieces as marked. With right sides together, pin and stitch the pockets in place. Fold the pockets away from the side seams and press.

tip.text: Transfer all notches and markings before removing the pattern pieces to make assembly easier.

steps.title: Assemble the Jacket Body
steps.content: Place the front jacket pieces onto the back piece with right sides together. Match the shoulder seams, pin and stitch. Press the seam allowances open. Repeat the process for the lining pieces. Align the pocket edges and stitch the front and back side seams together. Press the seams toward the front of the jacket. Match and sew the side seams of the lining in the same way.

tip.text: Be careful not to catch the pocket bags incorrectly in the side seams.

steps.title: Prepare and Insert the Sleeves
steps.content: Increase the stitch length and sew gathering stitches around the sleeve heads between the notches. Stitch the underarm seams of the sleeves with right sides together and press open. Pull the gathering threads gently to shape the sleeve caps. Match the sleeve notches to the armholes and stitch the sleeves into the jacket. Construct the sleeve linings in the same way and attach them to the lining armholes.

tip.text: Pull gathering threads gradually from both ends to distribute fullness evenly around the sleeve cap.

steps.title: Attach the Ribbed Waistband
steps.content: Fold the waistband ribbing in half lengthwise and stitch the short ends together to form a loop. Turn right side out and mark the quarter points. Match the quarter points of the ribbing to the jacket hem, aligning the centre back and side seams. Stretch the ribbing evenly as you stitch it to the base of the jacket.

tip.text: Do not stretch the jacket fabric itself; only stretch the ribbing while sewing.

steps.title: Construct and Attach the Cuffs
steps.content: Sew the short edges of each cuff together to create tubes. Fold each cuff in half lengthwise with wrong sides together. Match the cuff seam to the sleeve underarm seam and stitch the cuffs to the sleeve ends, stretching the ribbing evenly as you sew.

tip.text: Uneven stretching of the cuffs can create puckers around the sleeve openings.

steps.title: Attach the Ribbed Collar
steps.content: Fold the collar ribbing in half along the marked fold line. Align the centre back of the collar with the centre back neckline of the jacket. Pin around the neckline, clipping curves if necessary, and stitch the collar securely in place.

tip.text: Use plenty of clips around curved neckline sections to keep the collar evenly positioned.

steps.title: Insert the Zip
steps.content: Attach the right side of the open-ended zip to the right front edge of the jacket using a zip foot. Position the zip so the teeth sit close to the fabric edge and the tape faces inward. Repeat for the left side, ensuring both sides align correctly. Edge stitch the ribbing ends to the remaining exposed sections of the zip tape and secure the waistband base edges.

tip.text: Check zip alignment before stitching permanently to avoid uneven front edges.

steps.title: Join the Lining to the Jacket
steps.content: Turn the jacket right side out while keeping the lining wrong side out. Place the lining inside the jacket and align the front edges and neckline. Pin and stitch around the front opening and neckline, sandwiching the zip between the outer fabric and lining. Trim seam bulk and corners before turning the lining inside the jacket. Join the sleeve lining ends to the jacket sleeves, stretching the ribbing as required.

tip.text: Trim bulky seam allowances near the collar and zip for a smoother finished edge.

steps.title: Finish the Jacket
steps.content: Turn the jacket and lining inside out. Match the lower edges of the jacket and lining and stitch across, leaving a turning gap at the centre back of the jacket. Turn the jacket right side out through the opening. Slip stitch the turning gap closed and secure any remaining openings around the ribbing and zip corners. Press the jacket thoroughly to complete the project.

tip.text: Use a pressing cloth when ironing satin fabric to prevent shine marks or heat damage.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Gingham cotton fabric or another lightweight woven fabric suitable for making a small drawstring pouch

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description: Main fabric, lining fabric, drawstring cord or ribbon, matching thread, fabric marking tool, sewing needle or safety pin for threading the drawstring, and fabric scissors

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Cutting rounded fabric pieces, gathering fabric, sewing curved seams, attaching a gathered ruffle, constructing a lined pouch, turning through an opening, topstitching, sewing a drawstring casing, and threading drawstrings

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Pouch Body
steps.content: Cut two pieces of fabric measuring 4 inches × 6 inches. Round both ends of each 4-inch edge to create a curved shape.

tip.text: Stack the two fabric pieces together before trimming the curves so both pouch panels have matching shapes.

steps.title: Cut the Ruffle Strip
steps.content: Cut one fabric strip measuring 2 inches × 16 inches. This piece will be used to create the gathered ruffle.

tip.text: Cut the ruffle strip along the grain as evenly as possible to help the gathered edge sit smoothly against the pouch body.

steps.title: Gather the Ruffle
steps.content: Fold the ruffle strip lengthwise with the wrong sides together. Sew two parallel rows of gathering stitches along the raw edge, leaving long thread tails at both ends. Secure the threads at one end, then gently pull the thread tails at the other end to gather the fabric.

tip.text: Do not backstitch over the gathering stitches. Leave long thread tails so you can pull the threads and adjust the gathers evenly.

steps.title: Attach the Ruffle to the Pouch Body
steps.content: Mark the stitching points approximately 2 inches below each top edge of the pouch body. Place the gathered ruffle along the curved edge between the marked points, with the raw edges aligned. Adjust the gathers evenly and stitch the ruffle securely in place.

tip.text: Distribute the gathers evenly before sewing so the ruffle has a balanced, symmetrical appearance on both sides of the pouch.

steps.title: Sew the Main Pouch
steps.content: Place the remaining main fabric piece right sides together with the pouch panel that has the ruffle attached. Align the edges and sew around the sides and curved bottom. Leave the top opening unsewn.

tip.text: Keep the ruffle tucked inside the pouch layers while sewing so it does not get accidentally caught in the side or bottom seams.

steps.title: Sew the Lining
steps.content: Place the two lining pieces right sides together. Sew around the side and curved bottom edges, leaving the top edge open.

tip.text: Make sure the lining pieces are mirror-aligned before sewing so the curves match the shape of the main pouch.

steps.title: Join the Main Pouch and Lining
steps.content: Turn the main pouch right side out and leave the lining wrong side out. Place the main pouch inside the lining so the right sides are facing each other. Align the top edges and sew around the pouch opening, leaving a small opening for turning.

tip.text: Do not sew the entire top edge closed. Leave a turning opening large enough to pull the pouch through without stressing the seams.

steps.title: Turn the Pouch Right Side Out
steps.content: Carefully pull the pouch through the opening to turn it right side out. Gently shape the curved edges and push out the seams.

tip.text: Turn the pouch slowly and gently, especially around the curved seams, to avoid pulling or distorting the fabric.

steps.title: Close the Turning Opening
steps.content: Fold the raw edges of the turning opening inward. Topstitch around the top edge of the pouch to close the opening and create a neat finish.

tip.text: Press the top edge before topstitching to keep the seam flat and help the final stitching line look neat and even.

steps.title: Sew the Drawstring Casing
steps.content: Sew two parallel rows of stitching around the upper part of the pouch to create a channel for the drawstrings.

tip.text: Keep both stitching lines parallel and evenly spaced. If the channel is too narrow, the drawstring may be difficult to thread through.

steps.title: Insert the Drawstrings
steps.content: Thread one drawstring through the casing from one side and bring both ends out through the same opening. Thread the second drawstring from the opposite side in the same way. Tie the ends securely to complete the drawstring pouch.

tip.text: Attach a safety pin or bodkin to the end of each drawstring to guide it smoothly through the casing without twisting.

techPack.description: Cotton, quilting cotton, linen, lightweight canvas, or upcycled fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:

Drawstring cord
Thread

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Straight Stitching, French Seams, Topstitching, Drawstring Casing Construction, Cord Insertion

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Fabric
steps.content: Cut two fabric pieces measuring 7.9" x 6.3". Draw a guideline 1.5 inches below the top edge. Mark 3/8 inch from both side edges at the top opening area. Fold the side edges and top edges to the wrong side and secure them with clips.

tip.text: Press the folded edges before stitching to create crisp, even casings and cleaner side seams.

steps.title: Create the Drawstring Casings
steps.content: Sew along the folded edges to secure the side folds and top casings.

tip.text: Avoid stitching the casing closed at the side openings, or the drawstring will not be able to pass through later.

steps.title: Sew the Bag Using French Seams
steps.content: Place the two fabric pieces wrong sides together and secure with clips. Sew along both sides and the bottom edge. Trim the seam allowances. Turn the bag wrong side out and sew along the sides and bottom again to enclose the raw edges inside the seam.

tip.text: Trim the first seam allowance carefully before sewing the second seam, otherwise the raw edges may remain visible inside the finished bag.

steps.title: Insert the Drawstrings
steps.content: Turn the bag right side out. Cut two cords several inches longer than the bag opening. Thread one cord through both casings in one direction. Thread the second cord through the casings from the opposite direction. Tie the ends of each cord securely to create the drawstring closure and complete the project.

tip.text: Attach a safety pin to the end of each cord to make threading through the casing faster and easier.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Cotton, canvas, quilting cotton, or upcycled fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Cotton, canvas, quilting cotton, or upcycled fabric
One main fabric piece measuring 4.3" x 11"
One lining fabric piece measuring 4.3" x 11"
Snap fastener
Thread

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Straight Stitching, Turning, Topstitching, Snap Installation

steps.title: Cut and Prepare Fabric
steps.content: Prepare one main fabric piece and one lining fabric piece measuring 4.3" x 11". Seam allowances are included.

tip.text: Cut both pieces accurately to the same size so the edges align perfectly during sewing.

steps.title: Sew the Main and Lining Fabrics Together
steps.content: Place the main fabric and lining fabric right sides together. Sew around the edges, leaving a 1.5-inch opening for turning. Backstitch at both ends of the opening.

tip.text: Many beginners forget to backstitch at the opening, which can cause the seam to come apart when turning the project right side out.

steps.title: Trim Seam Allowances and Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Trim the seam allowances and turn the project right side out through the opening. Optionally add a small amount of stuffing to give the pouch a fuller shape.

tip.text: Trim close to the seam without cutting the stitches, as accidentally snipping the seam can create holes along the edges.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Fold the seam allowances of the opening inward and sew a topstitch close to the edge to secure the opening closed.

tip.text: Press the opening flat before topstitching to create a crisp edge and a more professional finish.

steps.title: Form the Pouch
steps.content: Fold the fabric lengthwise by approximately two-thirds to create the pouch body. Topstitch 1/4 inch from the edge along both sides and across the top.

tip.text: Uneven folding can result in a crooked flap or pouch body, so measure and align both sides before stitching.

steps.title: Attach the Snap Fastener
steps.content: Fold the remaining section down to create the flap. Mark the snap placement, install the snap fastener using the appropriate tool, and complete the closure.

tip.text: Double-check the snap placement before installing, as incorrectly attached snaps are difficult to remove without damaging the fabric.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Woven or upcycled fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Woven or upcycled fabric
Width 59": 0.5 yd
Width 45": 0.5 yd
Outer fabric: 1 piece, 20" x 18"
Lining fabric: 1 piece, 20" x 18" (same shape as the outer fabric after cutting)
Binding strip: 1 piece, 25.5" x 3"
Handle: 1 piece, 2.5" x 4"
All pieces include a 0.4" seam allowance unless otherwise noted.
Matching sewing thread
Pins or sewing clips
Fabric marker or tailor's chalk
Measuring tape
Scissors or rotary cutter
Iron and ironing board

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Pattern Cutting, Measuring and Cutting Fabric, Box Corner Construction, Straight Stitch Sewing, Lining Construction, Binding Attachment, Edge Stitching, Topstitching, Handle Construction, Pressing

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Outer Fabric
steps.content: Prepare one outer fabric piece measuring 20" x 18". Fold it in half along the 18" edge. Cut a 6" x 6" square from each upper corner.

tip.text: Measure both corner cutouts carefully so the finished storage bin stands evenly.

steps.title: Cut the Lining
steps.content: Cut one lining piece using the same shape and dimensions as the outer fabric.

tip.text: Stack the outer fabric and lining together before cutting to ensure both pieces match perfectly.

steps.title: Sew the Outer Bin
steps.content: Open the outer fabric. Place the right sides together and sew the adjacent edges of each cut-out square to form the box corners. Make sure the fabric is aligned before sewing.

tip.text: Match the cut edges precisely before stitching, or the base of the storage bin may become uneven.

steps.title: Sew the Lining
steps.content: Repeat the same process with the lining fabric to create the lining box.

tip.text: Keep the lining the same size as the outer bin to prevent wrinkles after assembly.

steps.title: Cut the Binding Strip
steps.content: Cut one binding strip measuring 25.5" x 3".

tip.text: Cut the strip with straight, clean edges to make attaching the binding easier.

steps.title: Join the Binding Strip
steps.content: Sew the two short ends of the binding strip together to form a continuous loop.

tip.text: Press the seam open after joining the strip to reduce bulk around the rim.

steps.title: Insert the Lining
steps.content: Keep the outer bin right side out and the lining wrong side out. Insert the lining inside the outer bin and align all side seams and corners.

tip.text: Make sure the lining is fully seated inside the outer bin before attaching the binding.

steps.title: Pin the Binding to the Top Edge
steps.content: Place the binding loop inside the top opening of the bin with the right side facing inward. Align the raw edges of the binding with the top edge of the bin and secure all layers with pins or clips.

tip.text: Distribute the binding evenly around the opening before pinning to avoid excess fabric at the end.

steps.title: Attach the Binding
steps.content: Sew all the way around the top edge to attach the binding, outer fabric, and lining together.

tip.text: Keep all three layers aligned while sewing to prevent the binding from twisting.

steps.title: Fold the Binding Outward
steps.content: Fold the binding upward and over the outside edge of the storage bin.

tip.text: Press the binding before topstitching to achieve a crisp, even edge.

steps.title: Press the Top Edge
steps.content: Press the top edge of the storage bin so the binding lies flat and the opening keeps its shape.

tip.text: Use steam while pressing to help the binding wrap smoothly around the rim.

steps.title: Topstitch the Rim
steps.content: Topstitch close to the seam around the top edge of the storage bin.

tip.text: Maintain an even stitching distance from the edge for a clean, professional finish.

steps.title: Finish the Binding
steps.content: Fold the remaining raw edge of the binding inward by approximately 0.2", then edge stitch close to the folded edge to secure it.

tip.text: Fold the binding evenly all the way around before stitching to avoid uneven widths.

steps.title: Cut the Handle
steps.content: Cut one fabric rectangle measuring 2.5" x 4" for the handle.

tip.text: Cut the handle along the fabric grain for added strength and durability.

steps.title: Sew the Handle
steps.content: Fold the handle piece in half along the 2.5" edge with the right sides together. Sew along the long edge.

tip.text: Use a consistent seam allowance so the finished handle has an even width.

steps.title: Turn the Handle Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the handle right side out through the opening. Press it flat, then optionally sew decorative topstitching along both long edges.

tip.text: Use a turning tool to push out the corners neatly without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Attach the Handle
steps.content: Position the handle on the outside of the storage bin according to the marked placement. Sew it securely using a square stitching pattern.

tip.text: Reinforce the handle with backstitching at each corner since it will bear the weight of the storage bin.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Medium-weight woven or upcycled fabric such as cotton, cotton canvas, cotton twill, or linen blend

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Medium-weight woven or upcycled fabric
Outer main panels: 2 pieces, 8.5" x 11.5" each
Outer side panels: 2 pieces, 4" x 6" each
Lining main panels: 2 pieces, 8.5" x 11.5" each
Lining side panels: 2 pieces, 4" x 6" each
Matching sewing thread
Pins or sewing clips
Fabric marker or tailor's chalk
Measuring tape or ruler
Fabric scissors or rotary cutter
Iron and ironing board

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Measuring and Cutting Fabric, Straight Stitch Sewing, Side Panel Construction, Rectangular Box Construction, Corner Sewing, Lining Construction, Layer Assembly, Turning Through an Opening, Edge Stitching, Topstitching, Pressing

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Fabric
steps.content: Cut 2 main body pieces measuring 8.5" x 11.5" each. Cut 2 side pieces measuring 4" x 6" each. Cut matching pieces for the lining so you have a complete set for both the outer cover and the lining.

tip.text: Cut the matching outer and lining pieces accurately to the same dimensions so both layers fit together evenly during final assembly.

steps.title: Attach the Side Panels to the Main Body
steps.content: Position one side panel at the center of the 11.5" edge of the main body piece with the right sides facing each other. Sew the pieces together to secure the side panel. Repeat on the opposite side.

tip.text: Mark the center of both the 11.5" edge and the side panel before pinning to keep the panel accurately centered.

steps.title: Sew the Side Seams
steps.content: Continue assembling the side seams of the cover with the right sides of the fabric facing each other. Sew the remaining main body section to the opposite edge of each side panel to form the rectangular corners. Repeat for all remaining sides.

tip.text: Avoid sewing past the corner points when joining the panels, as this can cause puckering and prevent the corners from forming clean right angles.

steps.title: Sew the Inner Cover
steps.content: Repeat the same construction steps used for the outer cover to assemble the lining, creating 2 matching rectangular cover layers.

tip.text: Use the same seam allowance for the lining and outer cover so the lining sits smoothly inside without excess fabric at the corners.

steps.title: Place the Two Layers Together
steps.content: Keep the outer cover right side out and the lining wrong side out. Insert the outer cover inside the lining so the right sides of both layers are facing each other. Align the upper raw edges and secure them with sewing clips.

tip.text: Match the corner seams of the outer cover and lining before clipping the remaining edges to prevent the layers from shifting out of alignment.

steps.title: Sew Around the Cover Opening
steps.content: Sew around the aligned raw edges of the cover opening, leaving a 2" section unsewn as a turning opening.

tip.text: Backstitch securely at both ends of the 2" turning opening so the seam does not pull apart while the cover is being turned.

steps.title: Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Turn the cover right side out through the 2" opening.

tip.text: Gently push out each corner with a blunt turning tool, taking care not to poke through the stitching.

steps.title: Close the Opening and Topstitch
steps.content: Fold the raw edges of the turning opening inward. Topstitch around the entire cover opening to close the gap and complete the project.

tip.text: Press the upper edge before topstitching and keep a consistent distance from the edge for a clean, professional finish.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Printed cotton fabric and plain cotton fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Printed cotton fabric
Plain cotton fabric
Matching sewing thread
4 buttons
Fabric marker or chalk
Pins or sewing clips

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Straight Stitching, Turning, Topstitching, Pressing, Folding, Button Attachment

steps.title: Cut and Sew the Fabric Square
steps.content: Cut one square from printed fabric and one square from plain fabric. For the large size, cut both squares at 11.8" x 11.8". Place the fabrics right sides together and sew around the edges using a 0.2-inch seam allowance, leaving an opening on one side for turning. Trim the corners, turn right side out, fold the raw edges of the opening inward, press, and topstitch around the entire square.

tip.text: Trim the corners diagonally before turning to reduce bulk and create crisp, sharp corners.

steps.title: Create the Fold Lines
steps.content: Fold the fabric square in half vertically and horizontally, pressing lightly to create two center crease lines. On the outside of the basket, mark the halfway point between the center and outer edge along each crease. Fold each corner diagonally from mark to mark and pin in place. Topstitch approximately 0.04 inch from the folded edge to create permanent creases.

tip.text: Inaccurate marking can cause the basket sides to become uneven, so measure each fold carefully before stitching.

steps.title: Form the Basket Shape
steps.content: Pinch one side of the square along the original pressed crease and pin a line from the corner of the base to the outer edge. Repeat on all four sides to form the basket walls. Topstitch along the pinned lines and flatten the corner pockets that are created.

tip.text: Press the folds before topstitching to help the basket hold its shape more neatly.

steps.title: Secure the Corner Flaps
steps.content: Fold down the corner flaps between the pockets. Sew a button through the flap and all fabric layers beneath it to secure the basket shape permanently. Repeat for all four corners to complete the origami box.

tip.text: Ensure the button placement is centered before sewing, as uneven placement can distort the shape of the finished box.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Printed cotton fabric, coordinating cotton fabric, and white cotton fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Printed cotton fabric
Coordinating cotton fabric
White cotton fabric
Lightweight fusible interfacing
Binding fabric strips (2" wide)
Matching sewing thread
Pins or sewing clips

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Template Tracing, Fusible Interfacing Application, Straight Stitching, Curved Edge Binding, Zigzag Stitching, Topstitching, Bias Binding, Hand Stitching

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Fabric
steps.content: Cut one background panel measuring 11.8" x 13.8" from printed cotton fabric. Fuse a matching piece of lightweight interfacing to the wrong side. Using the pocket templates, cut all pocket pieces from coordinating fabrics and fuse interfacing to the back of each pocket piece. Cut several binding strips measuring 2" wide from a darker coordinating fabric.

tip.text: Fuse the interfacing before cutting curved pocket edges to help maintain accurate shapes and prevent distortion.

steps.title: Bind the Pocket Curves
steps.content: Place a binding strip right sides together along the curved top edge of a pocket. Sew using a 0.2-inch seam allowance, easing the strip smoothly around the curve. Fold the binding over the raw edge, tuck under approximately 0.1 inch, and topstitch in place. Trim the excess binding. Repeat for all pockets.

tip.text: Avoid stretching the curved pocket edge while sewing, as this can cause rippling and uneven pocket openings.

steps.title: Attach the Pockets
steps.content: Arrange the pockets on the background panel according to the desired layout. Allow the top edges to flare slightly to create extra storage space. Pin in place and secure each pocket using a narrow zigzag stitch around the three straight sides.

tip.text: If the pockets are pulled flat while sewing, they may lose capacity and become difficult to use.

steps.title: Add Decorative Binding Strips
steps.content: Cut additional 2" binding strips. Apply them along the lower edges of the center pockets to cover the zigzag stitching. Fold the binding over the raw edge, tuck the seam allowance underneath, and topstitch neatly. Add another binding strip vertically down the center of the organizer to cover the remaining exposed stitching.

tip.text: Press the binding before topstitching to create crisp edges and a professional finish.

steps.title: Create Hanging Loops
steps.content: Cut two fabric strips measuring 0.8" x 4.7". Fold the long edges inward, fold each strip in half lengthwise, and topstitch close to both folded edges to create narrow hanging loops.

tip.text: Use a longer stitch length when topstitching narrow loops to achieve straighter, more even results.

steps.title: Attach the Hanging Loops
steps.content: Fold each loop in half and position them 0.4 inch from the top corners of the organizer with the loops facing downward. Secure them temporarily with a few stitches.

tip.text: Check that both loops are positioned at the same height before stitching to ensure the organizer hangs evenly.

steps.title: Add the Back Panel
steps.content: Cut a piece of white cotton measuring 11.8" x 13.8". Place it against the back of the organizer to cover all construction stitching and pin securely around the edges.

tip.text: Smooth the back panel carefully before pinning to prevent wrinkles from being trapped inside the finished organizer.

steps.title: Bind the Outer Edges
steps.content: Finish the entire outer edge of the organizer using 2" wide binding strips. Miter or overlap the corners neatly and fold all raw ends under before stitching. Topstitch around the perimeter to secure the binding.

tip.text: Take extra care at the corners to avoid bulky folds that can make the binding difficult to stitch evenly.

steps.title: Finish the Organizer
steps.content: Lift the hanging loops into an upright position and secure them with a few small hand stitches. Give the organizer a final press and complete the project.

tip.text: Press the finished organizer from the back side to avoid flattening the pockets and preserve their storage capacity.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Medium-weight cotton fabric for outer shell, lightweight cotton fabric for lining and appliqué motifs

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Medium-weight cotton fabric for outer shell
Lightweight cotton fabric for lining and appliqué motifs
Lightweight fusible interfacing
Fusible fleece
Fabric stabilizer
Matching sewing thread
Pins or sewing clips
Printed motif templates

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Template Tracing, Fusible Interfacing Application, Fusible Fleece Application, Appliqué, Free-Motion Embroidery, Satin Stitching, Straight Stitching, Box Construction, Turning, Topstitching

steps.title: Cut the Fabric Pieces
steps.content: Cut one square base and four side panels from outer fabric, lining fabric, and fusible fleece. For the small tub, cut one 6.7" square and four 6.7" x 7.9" rectangles. For the large tub, cut one 7.9" square and four 7.9" x 9.4" rectangles.

tip.text: Label the outer, lining, and fleece pieces immediately after cutting to avoid mixing them up during assembly.

steps.title: Prepare the Appliqué Motifs
steps.content: Trace the motif templates onto the paper side of fusible interfacing. Roughly cut out the shapes and fuse them to the wrong side of lightweight cotton fabric. Trim neatly around the motif outlines. Position the motifs in the center of the outer side panels, remove the backing paper, and press them in place.

tip.text: Make sure all motifs are centered before fusing, as repositioning them afterward may damage the fabric.

steps.title: Embroider the Motifs
steps.content: Outline each appliqué motif using free-motion embroidery, satin stitching, or hand embroidery. If using free-motion machine embroidery, lower the feed dogs, attach a free-motion foot, and place stabilizer beneath the fabric while stitching. Remove the stabilizer after completing the embroidery.

tip.text: Keep your stitching speed steady during free-motion embroidery to prevent uneven outlines and puckering.

steps.title: Attach the Fusible Fleece
steps.content: Fuse the fleece to the wrong side of all outer fabric pieces according to the manufacturer's instructions.

tip.text: Use a pressing cloth when fusing fleece to avoid scorching delicate fabrics.

steps.title: Construct the Outer Container
steps.content: Place two outer side panels right sides together and sew along one long edge using a narrow seam allowance. Press the seam open. Continue adding the remaining side panels until a tube is formed. Attach the square base to the bottom edge of the side panel tube with right sides together. Trim seam allowances and clip the corners.

tip.text: Clip the corners carefully after sewing the base to reduce bulk and help the box hold a crisp shape.

steps.title: Construct the Lining
steps.content: Repeat the same construction process with the lining pieces. Leave a 4" opening in one side of the base seam for turning later.

tip.text: Do not forget the turning opening, otherwise the project cannot be turned right side out after assembly.

steps.title: Join the Outer and Lining
steps.content: Turn the lining right side out. Place it inside the outer container so that right sides are facing each other. Match the raw top edges and sew completely around the top opening.

tip.text: Match the side seams carefully before sewing to keep the finished toy box symmetrical.

steps.title: Turn and Close the Opening
steps.content: Turn the entire container right side out through the opening left in the lining base. Fold the seam allowances inward and stitch the opening closed.

tip.text: Push out the base corners fully after turning to achieve a clean box shape.

steps.title: Finish the Toy Box
steps.content: Push the lining inside the container and press the top edge neatly. Topstitch around the entire upper edge. Fold the top edge down to create a decorative cuff and complete the project.

tip.text: Press the cuff thoroughly before topstitching to help the toy box stand upright and maintain its shape.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Assorted cotton fabrics and lightweight cotton lining fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Assorted cotton fabrics
Lightweight cotton lining fabric
Wadding
Pink bias binding
Decorative woven ribbon
Plastic boning (3.5-inch)
Matching sewing thread

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Template Tracing, Dart Sewing, Quilting, Straight Stitching, Circular Base Construction, Bag Construction, Lining Assembly, Turning, Boning Insertion, Topstitching, Bias Binding Application

steps.title: Prepare and Cut the Fabric
steps.content: Print the basket template and transfer it onto the fabric. Cut one outer basket panel, one lining panel, and one matching wadding panel. Transfer all dart markings onto the wrong side of the fabric pieces.

tip.text: Use a washable fabric marker to transfer dart markings accurately for a cleaner finished shape.

steps.title: Sew the Darts
steps.content: Fold each dart with right sides together and stitch from the raw edge toward the dart point. Repeat for all darts on both the outer fabric and lining pieces. Press the darts outward.

tip.text: Do not backstitch at the dart point, as this can create puckers and add unnecessary bulk.

steps.title: Quilt the Lining
steps.content: Trim the wadding around the dart areas and pin it to the wrong side of the lining. Stitch decorative quilting lines across the lining to secure the layers together.

tip.text: Start quilting from the center and work outward to prevent shifting and wrinkles in the wadding.

steps.title: Prepare the Circular Base
steps.content: Cut one fabric circle and one matching wadding circle measuring approximately 5.5 inches in diameter. Layer them together and secure with pins or clips.

tip.text: Use a circular template to keep the base perfectly round and easier to attach later.

steps.title: Construct the Outer Basket
steps.content: Fold the outer basket panel right sides together and sew the side seam. Attach the circular base to the lower edge of the basket body, easing the fabric evenly around the curve.

tip.text: Clip the curved seam allowances carefully without cutting through the stitching line to help the base sit flat.

steps.title: Construct the Lining
steps.content: Repeat the same process with the quilted lining piece. Sew the side seam and attach the circular base to complete the lining.

tip.text: Distribute the fabric evenly around the circular base to avoid puckers and uneven shaping.

steps.title: Join the Basket and Lining
steps.content: Place the outer basket right side out inside the lining, which should remain wrong side out. Align the side seams and top edges, then sew around the upper edge, leaving an opening near the back seam for turning.

tip.text: Remember to leave a turning opening, otherwise the basket cannot be turned right side out.

steps.title: Turn Right Side Out
steps.content: Pull the basket through the opening. Push the lining inside the basket and shape the top edge neatly.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to shape the curves and seams without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Add the Hanging Loop
steps.content: Fold a piece of ribbon into a loop and insert the raw ends between the lining and outer fabric at the back seam. Stitch securely to the outer basket.

tip.text: Reinforce the hanging loop with several rows of stitching to support the weight of the filled basket.

steps.title: Create the Boning Channel
steps.content: Stitch two vertical lines approximately 2 inches apart on either side of the back seam. Join them at the bottom with a horizontal line to form a channel.

tip.text: Mark the channel lines before sewing to keep the boning centered and straight.

steps.title: Insert the Boning
steps.content: Insert a 3.5-inch piece of plastic boning into the channel to help the basket hold its shape and prevent it from tipping forward.

tip.text: Ensure the boning is fully enclosed and the ends are smooth to prevent wear on the fabric over time.

steps.title: Finish the Top Edge
steps.content: Fold the remaining raw edges inward and topstitch around the entire opening. Apply bias binding around the top edge if desired for additional durability and decoration.

tip.text: Press the top edge thoroughly before topstitching for a crisp, professional finish.

items.name: Roll-Up First Aid Set
items.finishedSize:
First Aid Roll: 15 x 6.7 inches
Ouch Pouch: 5.5 x 5.5 inches

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Assorted cotton fabrics in coordinating colors and prints

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Assorted cotton fabrics in coordinating colors and prints
Wadding
Yellow herringbone ribbon
Elastic loop
1 button (0.8 inch)
Matching sewing thread
Embroidery thread
Fabric glue stick (optional)
Printable templates

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Template Tracing, Applique, Machine Embroidery, Straight Stitching, Topstitching, Quilting, Pocket Construction, Turning, Ladder Stitch, Button Attachment, Elastic Loop Insertion

steps.title: Prepare the Main Roll Panel
steps.content: Print and cut the templates. Cut a strip of bird-print fabric measuring 15 x 2.75 inches. Press both long edges 0.4 inches toward the wrong side. Position it across the center of a blue fabric panel measuring 15 x 6.7 inches.

tip.text: Press folded edges before stitching to achieve cleaner pocket openings and sharper edges.

steps.title: Create the Label Pocket
steps.content: Cut a yellow fabric rectangle measuring 2.4 x 3 inches. Fold it in half with wrong sides together and insert the raw edges beneath the upper edge of the bird-print band at a slight angle.

tip.text: Pin the pocket securely before stitching to prevent shifting and maintain an even angle.

steps.title: Stitch Decorative Details
steps.content: Topstitch both folded edges of the bird-print band. Stitch around the yellow pocket and embroider the words 'First Aid Rescue' onto the pocket using the tissue-paper transfer method.

tip.text: Avoid pulling embroidery stitches too tightly, as this may cause the fabric to pucker.

steps.title: Apply the First Aid Cross
steps.content: Cut a first-aid cross from red fabric. Position it on the front panel and stitch around the edges twice for durability.

tip.text: Use a shorter stitch length when appliqueing small shapes for smoother curves and cleaner edges.

steps.title: Prepare the Back Panel
steps.content: Cut a second blue fabric panel measuring 15 x 6.7 inches. Place it right sides together with the completed front panel.

tip.text: Match all corners carefully before sewing to keep the finished roll square.

steps.title: Add the Closure Ribbon
steps.content: Cut two pieces of ribbon measuring approximately 13.8 inches each. Finish one end of each ribbon by folding it under twice and stitching. Insert one ribbon between the front and back panels so the raw end extends beyond the seam allowance.

tip.text: Ensure the ribbon is positioned correctly before sewing, as it will be difficult to reposition after assembly.

steps.title: Assemble and Quilt the Roll
steps.content: Layer the project on top of a slightly larger piece of wadding. Stitch around the entire perimeter with a 0.4-inch seam allowance, leaving a turning opening. Trim corners and excess wadding, then turn right side out and topstitch around all edges.

tip.text: Trim the corners carefully without cutting the stitching line to reduce bulk after turning.

steps.title: Add Quilting Details
steps.content: Quilt around the bird-print panel, the first-aid cross, the yellow pocket, and selected decorative motifs.

tip.text: Quilting not only decorates the project but also stabilizes the layers for long-term use.

steps.title: Attach the Second Ribbon
steps.content: Lay the roll flat. Position the second ribbon approximately 6 inches from the right edge and stitch securely in place.

tip.text: Backstitch several times over the ribbon end to strengthen the closure.

steps.title: Create the Pocket Section
steps.content: Sew a yellow pocket panel and a blue pocket panel separately, turning and topstitching both pieces after construction.

tip.text: Leaving uneven seam allowances can cause the pocket layers to become misaligned.

steps.title: Divide the Pockets
steps.content: Place the blue pocket panel over the yellow panel and stitch vertical divisions to create small storage pockets.

tip.text: Mark pocket divisions with a removable fabric marker before stitching.

steps.title: Attach the Pocket Unit
steps.content: Position the completed pocket unit on the back of the roll and stitch vertical lines to create larger storage compartments.

tip.text: Make sure not to catch the closure ribbon while sewing the pocket divisions.

steps.title: Prepare the Ouch Pouch Front
steps.content: Cut an 8-inch square from bird-print fabric. Cut two coral strips measuring 0.8 x 8 inches and attach them across the center of the square.

tip.text: Use a washable glue stick or clips to hold narrow strips in place before stitching.

steps.title: Create the Ouch Label
steps.content: Cut the oval template from pale pink fabric and stitch it onto the coral strips. Embroider the word 'Ouch' using the tissue-paper method.

tip.text: Use contrasting thread colors to make the embroidered text easy to read.

steps.title: Mount the Decorative Panel
steps.content: Cut a blue fabric square measuring 5.5 x 5.5 inches. Position the completed bird-print square in the center and stitch around the edges.

tip.text: Check that the decorative panel is centered before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Construct the Pouch Body
steps.content: Cut a matching 5.5 x 5.5-inch backing piece. Place front and back right sides together and sew around the perimeter, trapping a small elastic loop in one corner. Leave an opening for turning.

tip.text: Keep the elastic loop fully inside the seam allowance to prevent accidental stitching errors.

steps.title: Turn and Topstitch
steps.content: Trim the corners, turn the pouch right side out, press carefully, and topstitch around the perimeter.

tip.text: Do not press directly on the elastic loop, as heat may damage or melt it.

steps.title: Fold the Pouch Shape
steps.content: Turn the pouch wrong side up. Fold the bottom corner and both side corners toward the center to create an envelope-style pouch.

tip.text: Use clips to hold the folds temporarily while checking the final shape.

steps.title: Hand Stitch the Sides
steps.content: Secure the folded side edges using ladder stitch to create the pouch compartment.

tip.text: Keep ladder stitches small and evenly spaced for a nearly invisible finish.

steps.title: Attach the Button and Finish
steps.content: Fold the top flap down, mark the button position, and sew the button securely in place. Test the elastic loop closure and complete the project.

tip.text: Sew the button firmly with multiple passes of thread since it will receive repeated tension during use.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Template Tracing, Fusible Interfacing Application, Straight Stitching, Box Corner Construction, Turning, Slip Stitching, Topstitching, Trim Attachment

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Pieces
steps.content: Print and cut out the template. Cut two outer fabric pieces, two lining pieces, and two interfacing pieces using the template. Fuse the interfacing to the wrong side of the outer fabric pieces according to the manufacturer's instructions.

tip.text: Allow the interfacing to cool completely before handling to ensure a strong bond with the fabric.

steps.title: Sew the Outer Fabric Body
steps.content: Place the outer fabric pieces right sides together. Match the edges marked A and sew using a 0.4-inch seam allowance. Then align the edges marked B and C and sew to form the pot shape.

tip.text: Carefully match the template markings before sewing, as misaligned seams can distort the final shape of the pot.

steps.title: Create the Boxed Corners
steps.content: With the outer fabric still wrong side out, press the seams flat. Pull apart the cut-out corner sections to form boxed corners and stitch across each opening using a 0.4-inch seam allowance. Turn the outer fabric right side out.

tip.text: Flatten the corner seams evenly before stitching to create a neat, symmetrical base.

steps.title: Construct the Lining
steps.content: Repeat the same construction process with the lining pieces. Sew the side seams, form the boxed corners, and leave the lining wrong side out.

tip.text: Press each seam after sewing to reduce bulk and improve the final finish.

steps.title: Insert the Base Support
steps.content: Cut a piece of plastic canvas mesh or sturdy card slightly smaller than the base of the pot. Place it inside the base of the outer fabric and secure it with a few hand stitches or fabric glue.

tip.text: Make sure the base insert is smaller than the seam allowances so it does not interfere with assembly.

steps.title: Join the Outer and Lining
steps.content: Place the outer pot inside the lining with right sides facing each other. Align the top edges and pin around the opening. Sew around the top edge, leaving a 4-inch opening for turning.

tip.text: Do not forget to leave the turning gap, otherwise the project cannot be turned right side out.

steps.title: Turn and Shape the Pot
steps.content: Turn the entire project right side out through the opening. Push the lining inside the outer fabric and carefully shape all corners and edges.

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to push out the corners without damaging the fabric.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Press the top edge flat and remove any wrinkles. Close the turning gap neatly using a slip stitch.

tip.text: Hand stitch with matching thread so the closure becomes nearly invisible.

steps.title: Topstitch the Upper Edge
steps.content: Topstitch around the entire top edge of the pot to secure the layers and create a crisp finish.

tip.text: Use a slightly longer stitch length when topstitching for a cleaner decorative finish.

steps.title: Attach the Pom-Pom Trim
steps.content: Hand sew or glue the pom-pom trim around the upper edge of the pot. Fold the top edge of the pot downward to reveal the lining and complete the project.

tip.text: If using fabric glue, allow it to dry completely before folding or handling the pot.

techPack.title: Techniques Required
techPack.description: Template Tracing, Machine Sewing, Hand Sewing, Segment Piecing, Turning, Stuffing, Sculpting with Thread, Felt Appliqué, Decorative Embellishment

steps.title: Cut the Pumpkin Segments
steps.content: Download and print the pumpkin template. Trace the pumpkin segment template onto eight fabric pieces using a variety of coordinating fabrics. Cut out all eight segments for one pumpkin.

tip.text: Arrange the fabric colors before sewing to create a balanced patchwork effect around the pumpkin.

steps.title: Sew the Segment Pairs
steps.content: Place two pumpkin segments right sides together and stitch along one curved edge using a 0.25-inch seam allowance. Finger-press the seam open. Repeat until four pairs are completed.

tip.text: Matching the curved edges accurately is important. Misaligned points can distort the pumpkin shape.

steps.title: Create the Pumpkin Halves
steps.content: Join two pairs together to create one half of the pumpkin containing four segments. Repeat to create the second half. Press all seams open.

tip.text: Press seams after each joining step to reduce bulk and create smoother curves.

steps.title: Assemble the Pumpkin Body
steps.content: Place both pumpkin halves right sides together and stitch around the outer edge, leaving approximately a 0.8-inch opening at the base for turning and stuffing.

tip.text: Do not sew the turning gap closed. The opening is needed for stuffing later.

steps.title: Turn and Stuff
steps.content: Turn the pumpkin right side out through the opening. Carefully shape the curves and fill firmly with toy stuffing until the pumpkin is evenly rounded.

tip.text: Understuffing can cause the pumpkin to collapse, while overstuffing may strain the seams.

steps.title: Close the Opening
steps.content: Hand sew the opening closed using small ladder stitches or whip stitches.

tip.text: Use matching thread and small stitches for an almost invisible finish.

steps.title: Sculpt the Pumpkin Segments
steps.content: Thread a long needle with doubled green embroidery thread. Insert the needle through the center top of the pumpkin and pull it through the bottom. Wrap the thread around the pumpkin between each segment, pulling slightly to create the characteristic pumpkin grooves. Repeat around all eight sections.

tip.text: Pull the thread firmly but not excessively, or the stuffing may become distorted.

steps.title: Create the Base Flower
steps.content: Cut the small flower shape from green felt. Sew a green button in the center and attach the felt flower to the base of the pumpkin, stitching through the entire pumpkin for stability.

tip.text: Stitch through the center of the pumpkin to help maintain the sculpted shape.

steps.title: Make Decorative Ribbon Curls
steps.content: Wrap ribbon around a cylindrical object and secure it. Apply craft glue and allow it to dry completely. Remove the curled ribbon and trim to the desired length.

tip.text: Allow the glue to dry fully before removing the ribbon to preserve the spiral shape.

steps.title: Attach the Ribbon Decoration
steps.content: Hand sew two curled ribbon pieces to the top of the pumpkin near the stem position.

tip.text: Position the ribbon curls before sewing to ensure they complement the pumpkin shape.

steps.title: Create the Stem
steps.content: Cut a piece of brown felt measuring approximately 1.4 inches x 2 inches. Fold it in half lengthwise, sew along the side and top edge, then stuff firmly to create the stem.

tip.text: Stuff the stem firmly so it remains upright when attached.

steps.title: Make and Attach the Leaf
steps.content: Cut a leaf shape from green felt. Make a slit at the center, insert the finished stem through the opening, and sew the stem securely to the leaf.

tip.text: Secure the stem with several stitches to prevent it from loosening during use.

steps.title: Finish the Pumpkin
steps.content: Position the felt leaf and stem assembly on top of the pumpkin and hand sew it securely in place. Adjust the ribbon curls and complete the pincushion.

tip.text: Take a few extra stitches through the center of the pumpkin to keep the embellishments firmly attached.

steps.title: Cut and Prepare the Fabric Pieces
steps.content: Download and print the templates. Cut the orange outer body pieces, taupe lining pieces, circular base pieces, ear pieces, eye appliqué, and quilt batting according to the pattern. Fuse quilt batting to the orange body and base pieces.

tip.text: Label each pattern piece after cutting to avoid confusion during assembly.

steps.title: Quilt the Outer Fabric
steps.content: Place each orange outer fabric piece on its matching quilt batting piece. Secure the layers together by zigzag stitching around the entire edge.

tip.text: Do not stretch the fabric while stitching or the outer tote may become distorted.

steps.title: Prepare the Appliqué Pieces
steps.content: Trace the eye pieces and inner ear pieces onto fusible adhesive web. Fuse them to the wrong side of the white fabric and carefully cut them out.

tip.text: Allow the fused pieces to cool before cutting for cleaner and more accurate edges.

steps.title: Construct the Fox Ears
steps.content: Cut two mirrored pairs of outer ears from orange fabric and one pair from batting. Baste one fabric ear layer to the batting, fuse the inner ear appliqué in the center, and secure it with a zigzag stitch.

tip.text: Center the inner ear appliqué carefully to keep both ears symmetrical.

steps.title: Sew and Turn the Ears
steps.content: Place the remaining ear pieces right sides together over the prepared ears. Stitch around the curved edges, leaving the bottom edge open. Trim the seam allowance, turn right side out, and press flat.

tip.text: Trim the seam allowance around curves before turning to reduce bulk and improve the ear shape.

steps.title: Attach the Fox Face
steps.content: Find the center of the padded orange body panel. Fuse the eye appliqué piece in place and secure it with a zigzag stitch around the edge.

tip.text: Use a matching thread color for the appliqué stitching to achieve a cleaner finish.

steps.title: Attach the Ears
steps.content: Position the completed ears along the top edge of the orange body panel, matching the raw edges. Baste them temporarily in place.

tip.text: Check that both ears angle outward evenly before stitching permanently.

steps.title: Join the Outer and Lining Top Edge
steps.content: Place the taupe lining panel over the orange outer panel with right sides together. Stitch along the top edge, securing the ears between the layers.

tip.text: Make sure the ears are fully tucked inside the seam allowance to prevent accidentally stitching through the visible ear section.

steps.title: Form the Tote Body
steps.content: Open the joined fabric layers and fold them in the opposite direction so the outer fabrics face together and the lining fabrics face together. Stitch the side seams, leaving a 2.75-inch opening in the lining seam for turning later.

tip.text: Press the top seam before sewing the side seams to keep the tote body aligned.

steps.title: Attach the Outer Base
steps.content: Pin the orange circular base to the bottom edge of the outer tote. Match opposite points first, then quarter points, before stitching around the entire circle.

tip.text: Distribute the fabric evenly around the circle to avoid puckers or gathers.

steps.title: Attach the Lining Base
steps.content: Repeat the same process with the taupe lining circle, stitching it to the lining section of the tote.

tip.text: Clip small notches into the seam allowance if needed to help the circular base sit smoothly.

steps.title: Turn the Tote Right Side Out
steps.content: Pull the entire tote through the opening left in the lining. Carefully shape the base and side seams until the tote stands evenly.

tip.text: Pull gently while turning to avoid stressing the circular seam allowances.

steps.title: Close the Lining Opening
steps.content: Fold the raw edges of the lining opening inward and close it neatly using a slip stitch.

tip.text: Use small hand stitches for an almost invisible closure.

steps.title: Topstitch the Tote Opening
steps.content: Push the lining inside the tote. Press the top edge and topstitch around the opening to keep the lining in place and create a clean finish.

tip.text: A slightly longer stitch length often produces neater topstitching on thicker layers.

steps.title: Add the Fox Face Details
steps.content: Sew two large round buttons onto the eye appliqué sections and attach a square button at the center as the fox nose. Complete the project.

tip.text: If the tote is intended for young children, replace buttons with embroidered details for added safety.
